review_title: Not high performance but not bad for the price...
review_text: Ive had this computer for a few months now and thought Id write a review on it. I rely heavily on reviews when purchasing electronics so this will be very detailed. If youd like the shorter version Ill leave a summery at the bottom.Ok so first thing first. I bought this computer for one reason only: to play Fortnite. That said, it has also become the main computer at home for both my wife and I. So, if youre not into Fortnite or games, this will hopefully still be helpful.When the computer first arrived, setup was easy however the computer was incredibly slow. Doing a quick inspection, I found a lot of bloatware on the device (not surprising). This was easily fixed by doing a clean install of windows OS (made easy by using the built in features in settings). Once the install finished I installed Fortnite and fired it up but the computer was still incredibly slow and Fortnite struggled to run at all even on the lowest settings. It was very jerky and playing competitively was nearly impossible. I also noticed a lot of other applications acting sluggish such as settings, various web browsers, explorer and mail. So heres what Ive done to improve performance!First, I went thru all the applications on the computer and deleted everything that I didnt need or didnt want to use. It was pretty easy to do in settings and had a small (but noticeable) impact on performance.The next thing I did was go thru all the settings with a fine tooth comb and tweak everything for optimal performance. The biggest settings I changed were around background applications but I literally went thru every setting even down to visual effects and transitions. This had a pretty noticeable impact on performance and made the computer feel less sluggish in general. A few other things I did, include changing it to high performance when plugged in (basically the opposite of power saver), turned off auto check for emails, removed the live tiles and I also disabled indexing for the main hard drive.This goes with the last one but things like antivirus, updates and defragmentation I turned off so they dont automaticity run. I still use all them (I am a firm believer in doing all the proper maintenance) but I have to remember to start them myself every night. This has helped because it means its not scanning my computer or downloading updates while playing or watching shows.Lastly, I went to Acers website and downloaded all the drivers for my device. Windows does this but not very well so I did it myself. That and installing the driver for the graphics card also had a big impact.As far as Fortnite (the reason I bought the computer in the first place), I went into settings and set everything to low except  view distance (set to max) and 3D resolution. I have it set to full screen (not windowed full screen). Ive noticed major improvements in performance. Its not where I could play at competition level but it is to where I can enjoyably play a casual game with friends and family. It lags very occasionally and Ive noticed slight delays when shooting sometimes and when trying to build quickly. These issues arent terrible and I still get plenty of kills but I do notice I play better on other devices.Ive tried other games and some of the older ones are playable but anything more intense then Fortnite wont play well at all.One other thing worth noting was I had issues with the screen flickering when playing games but that went away when I downloaded the drivers for the graphics card. I also have had issues with the mousepad and the number pad locking up but I reinstalled the drivers for those and so far no issues. Ill update this if they return.As far as the build quality, its cheap plastic. For the price what did you expect? ;) Still it looks sharp and has held up well.Two things I have not done but plan to do are to upgrade the ram and replace the hard drive with a solid state drive. There are two sticks of ram (4gb and 2gb). The 4gb one cant be replaced but the 2gb should be able to be upgraded. I havent confirmed this by opening it yet but thats what the description says and my research online confirms this. As for the SSD, it is something that can be interchanged but it sounds like its a little bit of work. Ill update this review if I do try it however I figured it would be more appropriate to share my experiences with it as it arrives rather then modified.In conclusion, this device is a good value for casual use such as email, web, Netflix, office, pictures and so on. But I would not advise it for anything beyond that unless you are willing to put in the time to optimize it and are comfortable with modifying advanced settings. I feel like (for the price) it is a good value, however, I will not be buying it again. Next time I will spend a little more to get something with more horsepower to suit my needs.

review_title: Incredible Deal, easy to upgrade to max performance.
review_text: This model (1TB HD, 4GB RAM) is the best buy in low budget laptops for many reasons. I was prepared to return it but it's exceeded my expectations. First, it has features almost never found in even sub $800 unit much less $329 - backlight keyboard, 1920 x 1080 display and upgradable/replaceable storage. For those reasons alone, it's a 5 star machine.It has a M2 slot accessible without violating warranty on bottom. I ordered it with $70 Crucial 275GB M2 SSD and additional 4GB RAM ($29) from Kingston (what it came with). So now for $429 I have a 15" Kaby Lake I3 with 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD and 1TB second drive with backlit keys and Full 1080p display and HD 620 Intel Graphics - better for video playback than 520. I could not find something close to this used much less new.And the other aspects are good as well. Keyboard is comfortable, number keybad is nice for my work, backlit works well (if on/off proximity function does not bug you, it does not me). Trackpad works better than I expected.Screen is a TN panel (1080P IPS would probably double the price). So viewing angles are not great and contrast is just okay. But for single person use it's good by budget panel features with better than expected color accuracy and a blue light filter that reduces strain.The chassis has a nice faux brushed metal look and more rigid than most sub $400 plastic models. Weight is so so - not heavy not light for a 15.6". Sound from speakers was also better than I expected in this price range.Bloatware on my model was minimal. BIOS is bare bones but easily accessible to change boot drive etc. And you get full ports without ultrabook dongles. And with my upgrades, model posted a 2900 Single Core Geekbench and 5800 multicore. Again, very good for a machine in this price range.I've had it for a week - will update long term use - but right now it's a winner. For the money, you can't find a better deal on a 15.6" HD with backlit.EDIT. Update. Everything is worked as stated above - nothing has changed. Battery life is impressive even with adding RAM and SSD. The only real quibbles is backlight timing is annoying and viewing angles are not ideal (not a great group laptop). But considering nothing at this prices even has backlight or 1080p screens, you would need to move to $500 or more model to improve. I would buy this again at the price without hesitation.

This laptop has exceeded my expectations from the start. I was looking for a lower end machine to do light audio editing and voice recording. After spending 20+ hours researching for a reliable laptop, I decided to jump on this top seller for Amazon. For $350, you are getting a lot of a machine. This Acer is able to be upgraded easily which will increase its usefulness in the future.So, here's my pro/con list.PRO:---Keyboard: The keyboard is fantastic to type on for long periods and the key spacing is perfect for people with larger hands. The keys aren't cramped and the layout seems just right. However, I would have preferred the delete key to be a little more obvious. I have accidentally hit the 'Home' button a few times. The keyboard is also backlit. This is a great feature for typing in the dark but I would have liked to see a bit more glow from the LEDs. I have heard that the keyboard covers that can be purchased for this model spread the light out a bit and make the backlighting look great.---CPU: Although it is an i3, this 7th gen CPU is more than capable of handling multiple demanding apps and light gaming (you won't be running any AAA graphically demanding titles on it, but light/moderate gaming and older titles should prove playable). There is little heat generated from this CPU while browsing the web or watching videos.---Screen: I prefer larger screens. The laptop I use for work is a Lenovo X240 with a 13" screen and 1280x768 resolution which looks terrible in comparison to this screen. Full 1080p HD resolution looks good on the larger 15.6" screen and the brightness is spot on. I am currently in a well lit room (no direct light on the monitor) and I have the brightness set all the way down and it is a very comfortable view while typing this review. I noticed that the viewing angles are fairly good when looking at the screen from the sides but not so much from above/below.---Ports: This thing has all the ports you'll need! USB 3.1 Type-C port is a huge bonus in making this machine future compatible with phones/monitors/etc. There are also 2 other USB 3.1 Type-A ports that boast super fast data transfer. The HDMI and VGA ports are great, although I think it is about time to kill off the VGA port.---Upgradability: You'll eventually want to add some RAM (at least 4GB) and this machine makes it easy to do just that. I haven't upgraded yet, still running fine on 4GB but will be purchasing an 8GB module soon for a total of 12GB. I'm not much of a multitasker and usually don't burn through RAM as much as the next guy, but I recognize that 4GB is pretty much the bare minimum nowadays. There is an M.2 SSD slot that is open and ready for a super speedy SSD (will be purchasing next week). This means that you can upgrade your system to run on an SSD without having to remove the 2.5" SATA HDD (which is a generous 1TB). You can also upgrade to a SATA SSD if you wish, but I believe you'll be happier going the M.2 route.CON:---HDD: The hard drive is 5400rpm and very slow. Boot times are around 1.5-2 minutes and reading large data sets is gonna take some time. This is the main reason I'll be updating to an M.2 SSD.---Trackpad: By far one of the touchiest track pads I have ever dealt with. I constantly am having to disable it by pressing Fn+F7 while typing. It does have a nice click to it but the cursor moves very erratically sometimes and I would recommend using a Bluetooth/USB mouse.---Speaker: Use headphones...that's all I'm going to say.So...even though I have a few things I dislike about the laptop, you need to look at the price. You are getting a lot of laptop for the low price of $350 and if you are just looking to do basic things and aren't into heavy gaming or video editing, this laptop may just be perfect for you.

review_title: Decent laptop with a few flaws
review_text: CPU: the i5 8250u processor will power-throttle under load - for most users this shouldn't be a problem but if you plan to game with it (and you probably will if you bought it for dedicated graphics) it might be an issue. You can use Throttlestop as a work-around and try undervolting to prevent it overheating.GPU: The MX150 is equivalent to the GTX 1030 desktop card. It is quite capable and will run games such as GTA 5 at 1080 at lower settings. It will struggle with newer games however and you will have to lower the resolution and settings to get a decent frame rate.SSD: 256 GB is quite small by today's standards and if you have a lot of files, you can either swap out the stock SSD for a larger capacity one or use an external drive. There is a spare bay on the bottom of the laptop but it is empty and you have to purchase the connection cables separate.Build quality: When I first bought the laptop, it would suddenly shut down without any warning when running on battery power. I found that this is a common fault on this laptop - the power safety cut-off switch inside the memory hatch is not held down firmly enough. A couple of layers of electrical tape fixed it for me.Screen: Definitely a weak point on this laptop. It is full HD (1080) but viewing angles are poor and colours look washed out.Overall: For the price, it is a decent laptop, despite these shortcomings. review_title: Maybe I was expecting too much?
review_text: To start, I will say this 2-in-1 does come with Intel Core I7 8th gen tech.I'm a casual computer user, mainly using it for web surfing, business, radio programming (I'm a radio nerd), and other general-use activities. I mulled it over a bit and eventually agreed that, in typical fashion, she was correct.  After exhaustive research, the specs on this one looked good - i7 processor for good speed, adequate RAM, a 2TD HD and a tablet.  The price was right as well so I pulled the trigger.I think I was expecting a race car but with the bloatware and background apps running, it really wasn't any faster than my old Dell.  Sure, on my Wi-Fi setup it had a smoking speed - 200+ MBs download on my 5GHZ network and 100+ on the regular, speeds my old laptop could not achieve - but it took too long to start up, was 'laggy' and there were times it would just completely stop responding while 'something' was running in the background.  Very annoying.  It works pretty well in tablet mode but, again, even starting a simple game like the pre-installed Candy Crush made the computer need to stop and think a bit before it would finally proceed.  What the heck?  On a side note here, I breifly thought about it before purchase but having a 17" tablet has pros and cons.  Pro - I don't need to use my readers as everything is large and crystal clear.  Cons?  Well, it's huge and a bit cumbersome plus it weighs over 6 lbs so take that into consideration.  As I type, I'm at my desk with a 24" LED screen plugged into the the HDMI port and a bluetooth speaker hooked up for sound.Anyway, I'm on my third day of ownership and as I pull more bloatware (I'm looking at you McAfee) and nanny programs out, it runs better and better.  Limiting the unnecessary start-up's is also speeding things up nicely.  With some work, this 2-in-1 will become quite a nice laptop but you will need to do a little clean-up.  I would recommed it but if your not the type who 'modifies' things, expect some annoyances.  I was originally going to give it 3 stars just from the aggravation but as I use it more, I'm going to bump to 4.

review_title: Fantastic compromise between tablet and laptop
review_text: I recently bought a Lenovo X1 which came with a smart pen. I didn't buy the laptop for that feature. In fact I didn't discover the pen until the unit arrived at my house. But I tried it, and I now love handwritten notes.I was headed out into the field for work in an unstable foreign country and didn't want to risk losing my new X1. So I looked at cheap tablets that included styluses. I tried two but was disappointed with both of them. Then I saw this "Book". For the purpose of taking handwritten notes, this Book serves just as well as my X1, only it is super thin, lightweight, and if I lose it, I am out $340 instead of $2k. Highly recommended.There are two major drawbacks that you should know about, however. The first is that it has only one USB port, and this port is used for both charging of the unit, and for USB (requires on-the-go dongle, not included). Result: no charging while using the USB port. I haven't tried any of the charging OTG adapters because this laptop features rapid charging (12Vdc through USB port rather than 5Vdc) and I am afraid that these cheap adapters will end up putting 12 volts onto my 5V USB devices.The second drawback has to do with the Real Pen. It has no shortcut button. On my X1 laptop, the pen has a button on the side of the barrel that when pressed switches your pen from ink to eraser. With the Book's Real Pen, if you make a mistake while writing, you have to move up to the tool bar, select the eraser, erase your error, then return to the toolbar to pick up a pen. PITA, compared to not having to move your arm on the X1. As far as I know, there are no alternate pens to buy for this unit even though I understand that the writing tablet is made by Wacom.Overall I love it and take it wherever I go. I only wish I had found the Book before I found the X1! I might have saved a bundle of cash.

review_title: There is NO BETTER VALUE in laptops....Period!! I stake my 20 hours of research on it! ACER killed it with this one!
review_text: Let me paint a picture:My background is in purchasing, I am a research nerd. I used to spend in excess of 50 million a year for the largest retailer of its kind in my industry, I am obsessive when comparing details and am even more obsessed with getting every last ounce of value for my money. I am not the most tech savvy person you will ever meet, but I believe I am above average, and I also believe I am a realistic person with regards to my expectations. This is a fantastic laptop for the majority of people, I do not intend to do heavy gaming or run heavy/complex programs. This laptop is like the F-150 of laptops (sorry Chevy fans) , yes some people need an F-250 or even F-350 for towing/hauling, but for most people an F-150 is all they will ever need.With that said, I spent about 20 working hours comparing over 400 laptops (nerd) from all major brands, and looked at over 300 deals(super nerd) offered on laptops by all major retailers on both black friday and cyber monday. I chose this laptop for $329 on cyber monday, and although it was only $20 off, versus others that were $200 or more off, this was still the most computer for the money.Here is why to buy this laptop:1)  Newest Kaby Lake generation 7 Intel processor, low 15 watt usage and great speed for the price. Runs quiet and cool.2)  DDR4 ram, again the latest and greatest, also happens to be the cheapest ram available. Ram prices have an inverse relationship to normal consumer priced goods. Most things cost more when new, but because PC components become obsolete so quickly, when ram is first introduced this is the product being currently manufactured, which in turn means supply can easily exceed demand, which means lower prices. Once ram is no longer being actively manufactured the supply dries up and prices increase. Also ram can EASILY be added to this laptop, takes less than 5 minutes and costs exactly $24.99 for the best available, here is the link to the 4GB stick I added: https://www.amazon.com/Ballistix-16GBx2-PC4-19200-SODIMM-260-Pin/dp/B01DGOF6GE?th=1 ***Additional note about ram, I chose to purchase an additional stick of 4gb rather than a 8gb or 16gb.  There is a phenomenon known as "dual channel" with regards to ram, the concept is that if you have 2 like sticks of ram (they need to match in a few tech specs), in the exact same size, ie: 2 sticks of 4gb of ram, your pc will be able to access both sticks of ram at the same time. If you have 2 mismatched sticks, like a 4gb and an 8gb, then the pc will access only 1 at a time. Therefore after talking to a computer genius friend of mine and doing about an hours research on this specific application, my best guess is that the extra money on the 8gb stick of ram would be a waste, two 4gb sticks of dual channel ram will out perform a 4gb and 8gb stick together for most applications. Also please note that for 99% of users 8gb of ram total is plenty. My personal opinion of adding more than 8gb of ram to this specific laptop would be like putting the most expensive Z rated tires on your honda accord, yes the tires might be rated for 200mph, but will you ever utilize it? If you do want to have more than 8gb of ram total, I would recommend purchasing 2 identical sticks of 8gb or 16gb ram to utilize dual channel.3)  Full 1080 HD LED back lit (vs LCD) Screen, pretty much unheard of for this price. LED backlit biggest advantage is it uses less energy, thus better battery life.  Also has a matte finish screen, I prefer the look of a glossy screen (good for a desktop in a controlled lighting environment), but because laptops travel with you to different places, you often times have reflection problems with a glossy screen.4)  Battery life, best battery life you can get for anywhere close to 3x the cost of this pc. Please know that 12 hours is in best case scenario, meaning lowest screen brightness, and NOT playing videos or games or other CPU intensive tasks. Based on my first week of use I feel comfortable planning on a solid 7 to 10 hours of normal use. Please note that the battery is not easily removed, as one reviewer put, "let your future self worry about that". ****Note on battery, ACER has a specific process for breaking in your battery. If you do not follow it you WILL limit its potential. If you are too lazy to find the manual online here is my summary of what they say: Charge laptop to full (charge light turns to blue) before you ever turn it on. Then leave the laptop plugged in while the computer updates, it will not update and boot up the first time without being plugged in. As soon as updates are completed unplug the laptop and use the PC until the battery is almost dead. Then charge it to full and immediately unplug and discharge to near empty. Do this cycle a total of 3 times to condition your battery for its best longevity.5) Back LIT keyboard, there is no other laptop back of $800 that offers a backlit keyboard that I could find. This means the keys light up when one is pushed, you will absolutely love this feature if you have never had it. Also the keys are crisp but very easy to use, I love them.6) Easily upgrade-able. I will briefly touch on this, because other reviews have done a fine job of addressing it. Basically to turn this PC from great to ridiculously amazing do 2 things. The first is add ram (although mine operated for almost a week very well on the stock 4GB). The second is add a SSD or Solid State Hard Drive. To make a long story short the motherboard for this PC has 2 spots for a hard drive, the SATA and the m.2. The 1TB stock hard drive is installed on the sata slot. That means the m.2 slot is open. You can either purchase a traditional sata SSD and replace the existing hard drive, or purchase a m.2 SSD and have 2 hard drives. The latter is the option I chose, I am placing the operating system and programs on the SSD because it is much quicker, and I will place files (Photos, games, music, movies) on the stock drive. ***If you decide to pull the stock hard drive, you can purchase a usb case for it and turn it into an external hard drive that connects via usb cable.7) Newest AC wifi technology for fastest speeds8) All the other tech stuff you want like usb 3, hdmi, CD RW drive, blah blah blah.9) Fit and finish is excellent. Speakers are also stupid good for this price range.Reason's to not buy:1) You need more of a workhorse PC2) You print money in your basement and don't care about value3) You don't like Henry Fords philosophy of "you can have any color you like as long as it is black", because this PC only comes in the 1 color.Conclusion: Sometimes, and much more rarely than you would think, a manufacturer actually listens to customers and gives them everything they want at a great price.  This laptop is a unicorn in the fact that it has ALL SOLID FEATURES, with 2 potentially weak spots for some users (ram and hard drive). But these are easily upgraded, and the truth is (regardless of what tech nerds might argue), 4gb of ram, and the included hard drive are more than adequate for the majority of users. The only real question you have to ask yourself is do you have the patience to wait, or will you pony up for 1 day shipping?

This laptop has exceeded my expectations from the start. I was looking for a lower end machine to do light audio editing and voice recording. After spending 20+ hours researching for a reliable laptop, I decided to jump on this top seller for Amazon. For $350, you are getting a lot of a machine. This Acer is able to be upgraded easily which will increase its usefulness in the future.So, here's my pro/con list.PRO:---Keyboard: The keyboard is fantastic to type on for long periods and the key spacing is perfect for people with larger hands. The keys aren't cramped and the layout seems just right. However, I would have preferred the delete key to be a little more obvious. I have accidentally hit the 'Home' button a few times. The keyboard is also backlit. This is a great feature for typing in the dark but I would have liked to see a bit more glow from the LEDs. I have heard that the keyboard covers that can be purchased for this model spread the light out a bit and make the backlighting look great.---CPU: Although it is an i3, this 7th gen CPU is more than capable of handling multiple demanding apps and light gaming (you won't be running any AAA graphically demanding titles on it, but light/moderate gaming and older titles should prove playable). There is little heat generated from this CPU while browsing the web or watching videos.---Screen: I prefer larger screens. The laptop I use for work is a Lenovo X240 with a 13" screen and 1280x768 resolution which looks terrible in comparison to this screen. Full 1080p HD resolution looks good on the larger 15.6" screen and the brightness is spot on. I am currently in a well lit room (no direct light on the monitor) and I have the brightness set all the way down and it is a very comfortable view while typing this review. I noticed that the viewing angles are fairly good when looking at the screen from the sides but not so much from above/below.---Ports: This thing has all the ports you'll need! USB 3.1 Type-C port is a huge bonus in making this machine future compatible with phones/monitors/etc. There are also 2 other USB 3.1 Type-A ports that boast super fast data transfer. The HDMI and VGA ports are great, although I think it is about time to kill off the VGA port.---Upgradability: You'll eventually want to add some RAM (at least 4GB) and this machine makes it easy to do just that. I haven't upgraded yet, still running fine on 4GB but will be purchasing an 8GB module soon for a total of 12GB. I'm not much of a multitasker and usually don't burn through RAM as much as the next guy, but I recognize that 4GB is pretty much the bare minimum nowadays. There is an M.2 SSD slot that is open and ready for a super speedy SSD (will be purchasing next week). This means that you can upgrade your system to run on an SSD without having to remove the 2.5" SATA HDD (which is a generous 1TB). You can also upgrade to a SATA SSD if you wish, but I believe you'll be happier going the M.2 route.CON:---HDD: The hard drive is 5400rpm and very slow. Boot times are around 1.5-2 minutes and reading large data sets is gonna take some time. This is the main reason I'll be updating to an M.2 SSD.---Trackpad: By far one of the touchiest track pads I have ever dealt with. I constantly am having to disable it by pressing Fn+F7 while typing. It does have a nice click to it but the cursor moves very erratically sometimes and I would recommend using a Bluetooth/USB mouse.---Speaker: Use headphones...that's all I'm going to say.So...even though I have a few things I dislike about the laptop, you need to look at the price. You are getting a lot of laptop for the low price of $350 and if you are just looking to do basic things and aren't into heavy gaming or video editing, this laptop may just be perfect for you.

The constant interruption to my studies thanks to these issues is unacceptable. I gave Dell the benefit of the doubt for the first build quality problem, then again when the order was mixed up and I was sent two laptops instead of one, then again when the computer's performance was stuttering doing light web browsing, then again when the battery began to last 2 - 4 hours. But I cannot extend understanding anymore and assume I was just unluckily sent a defective unit.It's not difficult to envision how these issues could (and most likely will) continue until my computer is out of warranty and the onus is on me to fix it. I used to love dell and my first desktop was an Alienware tower, but after this experience, I will never be buying a Dell product again (and strongly persuading my friends to follow suit).Save yourself the hassle and do not buy this product.

review_title: Good gaming, at a good price.
review_text: -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Final Update (June 8, 2019)(said I would after a few months of use):-Still no complaints, laptop has been rock steady, have not had a single "crash" since purchase.-Still one of the quietest laptops Ive had recently, fans are virtually silent. Obviously they'll spin up during graphics intensive games or when you are doing considerable multi-tasking with a heavier load on cpu/gpu. Also, as always, periodically get some canned air to clean out the vents, etc.-Have had one odd anomaly, laptop has entered sleep mode on its own, during gaming sessions. Checking the windows event viewer, this appears to be graphics related. Unfortunately it could be anything, from cooling issues, to drivers issues, game coding glitches, or windows build glitches. The system doesn't actually crash, it just goes to sleep, so its hard to pin down.-Still cant give you any info on the battery. It works, but as mentioned initially it is a UPS for me, and thankfully I haven't had any long term power outages (knock on wood).-I see the price of this model has come down, and ASUS has introduced a couple models (more expensive) with newer graphics, increased factory storage, etc, so you have some options now.*Ultimately, I do not regret this purchase, it was, and is, still a really nice gaming laptop, especially for those dedicated to the AMD side of the equation.*I have no plans to further update this review, but if something major happens, an unknown flaw rears its head, or I figure out the sleep issue, Ill go ahead and note it here.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Disclaimer. This is an initial review and I will update it over time as needed, having had the laptop for a little over a week (Mar. 10, 2019)OVERVIEW: Though Intel and Nvidia make good products that can provide a lot of performance, both have increasingly come at a premium as the years progressed. I know that there are others out there, who like me, intentionally stick with AMD products. Their price for performance is consistently better, and they provide the only competition that keeps the Intel/Nvidia duopoly from becoming criminally expensive.BATTERY DISCLAIMER: I have given the battery 5 stars, not because its good (or bad), but because it is an aspect I cant evaluate properly. For me, this laptop is essentially a desktop replacement, the battery's primary purpose is as a UPS (uninterrupted power supply) in the event of a power outage. When this occurs, or the infrequent times I travel overnight and take the laptop, Ill update the battery life evaluation.PROS:-Good size for 15.6, no thick bezels, lightweight compact chasis-Boots in a few seconds thanks to the M.2 NVME SSD-Easy to upgrade, take screws off bottom, pop it off, full access-Has slot ready to go for a traditional 2.5" SSD (or HDD) alongside the existing M.2, includes mounting screws-Initial bootup had firmware update available and completed through Windows Update (nice touch for the less tech savvy)-Uses AMDs newest, high performance, low power draw, mobile cpu, designed for mobile gaming, etc-Quiet, like dead quiet with basic tasks, and even when gaming the fans aren't that loudNEUTRAL:-With falling memory prices its almost inexcusable this didn't include at least a 512 M.2, or secondary storage drive-Same as a above, for minimal cost this could have included double the RAM-The 560 is an aging graphics platform, this version (560X) is a marginal upgrade and does include 4GB RAM though-Above I stated lightweight, while nice, I am not sure if this is design intentional or reflective of cost cutting, I am not sure how this would handle a waist high drop-Screen, while good, is still a 15.6, you will want to attach an external monitor for long term use. Laptop screen defaults to a "zoomed" in view due to it  being 1920x1080, which can effect some programs.NEGATIVE:-Limited ports, 3 USB, 1 HDMI, 1 Audio, 1 Ethernet. Get yourself a USB HUB, you'll likely need it.-Its standard today, the battery is built in. It helps on space saving designs (as noted above though, replacement appears like it would be easy because for the most part removing the bottom gives you full interior access)-Attracts fingerprints on the inside (track pad and surrounding areas, etc)*Like I said above, this is an initial review, to give prospective buyers something to chew over if they are considering this machine. I will update this in a few months when I have a better feel for the overall experience. In the meantime, I have no complaints, I received a good machine at a good price, and the few games I have played (like OVERWATCH) were an enjoyable experience. Bear in mind this is not a $2000 gaming laptop, and reign in over-expectations. This will likely play any game out, but you may have to tinker with the graphics a little bit for optimal performance.

Display flexes, do not grab this computer by the display.-Could use an extra 2 USB ports or even more with all the space on the case and on the back; weighs enough to which it's questionable as to why it doesn't have an optical disc drive-Fairly middling colors on the display; light bleed near the webcam on a black screen.-Dell warranty repairs sometimes can be harrowing, according to forums, if needed-Red backlighting looks a bit gaudy, keys are red as well which has poor visibility with backlight off-The maintenance hatch was not fully flush when I received the item. review_title: I have had my current HP for 7 years and it has always performed nicely. I bought a Lenovo 3 years ago as ...
review_text: I decided to buy another HP to replace my current HP. When I started looking for a computer I was looking at metal chassis machines for durability. I travel a lot and use my computer on planes, trains, in coffee shops, malls, and sometimes in my office. I have had my current HP for 7 years and it has always performed nicely. I bought a Lenovo 3 years ago as a replacement because my HP was starting to slow down and I am impatient. The screen developed a line across it just after a year. Multiple screws fell out of the case and it started getting buggy. I switched back to my HP and it performed without any problems. The more I researched the more I went back to HP.When I received the package the outer box was undamaged but the original box the computer was packed in had significant damage and my first thought was I had to return it. The second thought was why would they ship a computer in a box with that much damage. I took pictures and prepared to return the computer. I travel a lot for work and do not spend much time in the United States and the next time I will be in the country is in June of 2018 so I thought if the computer works and is not damaged I will keep it. I took the computer out of the packaging and there were no visible signs of damage. I plugged it in and started it up and everything worked just like it should. Everything is tight with no scratches.The computer is light and looks like it has a metal chassis. It feels solid and not flimsy like some other brands. About 2 hours after I finished setting it up I stepped outside for a minute and my granddaughter pulled the computer off the table onto the hardwood floor. She did not get hit with the computer and my wife quickly moved her to another room and picked up my computer. She was afraid it was broken. After looking the computer over the only damage is to one of the corners. The computer is still solid, and works just fine. I am very happy with it and will look at HP again next time I buy a computer.I timed the battery life and with normal use with no gaming and only light video streaming it lasted more than 8 hours. I expect the time to go down some over time but if I get half the performance I got out of my old HP I expect the battery to last during most of my out of office time and during all but the longest flights.I only gave 4 stars because the damage done to the box. There were three items in the Amazon box when it arrived and this one was in the middle so it was not damaged in transit. It had to be damaged prior to shipping.

review_title: One of the best choices in the market today for on the go gamers who value a professional looking laptop!
review_text: Being one of the first reviews on a product is a hefty responsibility and as such I will do my best to give you the information that I know I would want when first looking at buying a specific laptop. To summarize for those looking for less info, I absolutely recommend this laptop to anyone and everyone who is looking for a lightweight, portable, powerful gaming laptop that is as versatile as it is cool! To begin the long review, Ill give you a little background on my experience in this area:I am an avid gamer and I have owned 4 different gaming laptops: the 2016 HP Omen, 2016 Razer Blade 14 1060, the 2016 MSI GS63VR-Stealth Pro-001, and I am now the proud and happy owner of the 2017 MSI GS63VR-Stealth Pro-230. I have tried the previous three models and I like them all, but this one is seriously an amazing creation to behold.For ease of reading, I will bullet point and explain my favorite things about this laptop.-It is one of the lightest and thinnest gaming laptops on the market.This laptop weighs less than 4 pounds and is thinner than a nickel is tall. It is actually lighter than my end of 2016 model Razer Blade 14 and just as thin. Logically, that just shouldnt make sense, right? A 15.6 laptop with full keyboard weighing LESS than a 14 laptop with no number pad? Crazy. Chalk this up to material quality or whatever you like, but I have owned both laptops and find both to be superb feeling, high quality machines.-It has an incredible selection of input and output options.This laptop boasts a staggering variety of I/O ports that are bound to fulfil your needs. It has three USB 3.0 ports, one USB 2.0 port, one thunderbolt 3 port, an SD card reader, separate premium jacks for headphones and a microphone, Mini Display Port, HDMI, Ethernet, and a Kingston lock slot. Need I say how awesome this is? Whereas the Razer Blade and MacBook Pro at this price are simply anemic in the way of ports, this beast has loads and still manages to fall in the same weight and thickness class as the aforementioned competitors at this price. A couple things to note though: The SD card reader is only 2.0 USB speed last I checked, so you will want a dongle if you want 3.0 USB transfer speeds for your SD cards. The other thing is that the HDMI is the 1.4 and not latest 2.0 edition, so it can only push 4K video at 24fps (this is fine for watching movies but for games you will want to use the thunderbolt or other options as they become available to get faster frame rates on a 4K monitor or TV). Aside from these two small inconveniences, this thing is ready and raring to be the center of your gaming and media editing workstation experience!-Looks and feels amazing!After having owned the 2016 Razer Blade 14, I thought nothing else in the PC world would satisfy me again in the way of build quality and solid feel. This Stealth and the last-year model have matched it in my opinion. The sleek finish and slightly edgier appointments like the red accents and dragon logo serve this laptop well. Quick story and you can believe it or not: I was studying in a bar late one night because that was all that was open that late, and this cute blond bartender looks over at me and my laptop and says, Is that a Ferrari laptop?? She mistook the symbol for the Ferrari logo at that distance!! Thatll cheer up anybody on a low day. Later, she brought me my beer and enthusiastically complimented the rainbow backlighting too; total nerd win!!! This thing is a pleasure to hold, a pleasure to carry, and is easy on the eyes to boot.As for more about the feel, the SteelSeries keyboard is just legendary. The typing action and depth is smooth and I have thus far experienced no fatigue while typing up research papers and gaming. The silver lining color scheme of the unlit keys is awesome because it makes them distinct from one another during the daytime without the backlight on, which is a great feat for an all-black color scheme. I have owned Samsung, Razer, HP, and Apple laptops, and this is my favorite keyboard I have typed on so far. The font can be a little jarring at first, but you get used to it. Some of the key positions are shifted away from what is normal too, but once you get used to it everything is smooth sailing. For example, on HP laptops there are dedicated buttons for volume up and down. On this, you hit the FN key and then press the up and down arrows, but believe it or not this works well! The FN button is used with a few other keys to control the volume, keyboard brightness, screen brightness, and volume, and it works very well. In fact, I kind of like not having to take my palms off their resting places to adjust those settings like I used to. I love the keyboard backlighting as well and the Dragon Center application makes it a breeze to change the colors and patterns in the 3 customizable zones to suit your fancy.-Runs like a beast, games like a beast, much better than last years models!I wont go too much into the specifics here as there are a plethora of excellent YouTube channels and blogs that can tell you what the NVidia 1060 and Intel 7th generation I7-7700HQ processor can do. What I will tell you is that speed is no longer a thing that crosses my mind as an issue anymore. This 2017 Stealth is such a better deal than the old 001 model on Best Buy for several reasons. First of all, it has an SSD that is PCIe as opposed to simple SATA. As such, it is pants-sizzling fast. The 2TB Hard drive is a great feature as well. Being as picky as I am, though, I swapped it out with a 500 GB Samsung 850 EVO SSD. In doing so, I shaved a couple more ounces off the weight and I now have two installed hard drives with no moving parts which is much better longevity speaking since I travel with this computer every day. However, I kept the 2TB hard drive and put it in an external closure to become my new external hard drive! That is a win-win in my book folks! Another way that it is superior is its panel. Full HD IPS here, folks, no budget panels on this 1.5K+ laptop!!To sum this review up, I am including a Question and Answer section that I hope will address some common concerns:Q: Is the power buttons weird placement going to make me put it into sleep mode all of the time if I bump into it?A: No. There is a simple setting tweak in Windows Power Options where you can turn the 1-click sleep mode off. I can click and bump the button all day and it will not go to sleep. If I want to put it to sleep, I just select it from the menu or press FN+F12 as MSI seemed to have the foresight to program this into their FN selection (even though they didnt have the foresight to move the button from such a dumb location).Q: Does this get covered in fingerprints?A: Kind of, it is less oleophilic than the finish of the Razer Blade 14, but fingerprints can accumulate over time. Just keep it wiped off and the appearance will be maintained.Q: Are the fans loud and whiny?A: Only when gaming. Basic physics tells us that smaller objects traveling at high speed will emit higher pitched sound than larger objects traveling at the same speeds. This is a small laptop with small fans, as such it will be loud and whiny when under load, but consider this a blessing from the thermodynamic gods at MSI since it keeps your PC from overheating. What is great though, is that the Dragon Center app allows you to customize the fan speed and fan curve as needed. Moreover, the GPU and CPU each have their own dedicated fan systems, 2 fans and 1 fan respectively, so that there will only be as many fans turned on as is necessary. The fan speed control option is great too as it allows you to select a mode called Cooler Boost in which both sets of fans run at max speed to keep your system as cool as possible. This is an awesome feature for those extended gaming sessions. Conversely, you can turn down the fans or flat out turn them off if you wish to be as stealthy as the laptops name implies; just dont burn up your CPU or GPU for the sake of quietude.Q: Does the MSI Stealth get hot?A: The answer to this has to do with the answer above, the fans do an excellent job of keeping the temperatures down and the Dragon Center app monitors exact temps for both the CPU and the GPU in real time. As such, I have never encountered temperature readings over 72C when doing heavy gaming and it usually idles between 29 and 40 degrees celsius. Under normal web browsing and school uses I get between 30C and 50C temperatures depending on what I am doing. Your experience may vary, though. The felt covering on the bottom of the laptop also does an excellent job of keeping the heat off of your tender parts when doing video editing or gaming from a laptop position. :DQ: Are the Power cord/ port positions on the right side annoying?A: Personally, not very, but I can see how they could be. If you for some reason had thunderbolt, power, mini display port, HDMI, and USB running all at once or in a lower number combination thereof, you could say goodbye to comfortably using a mouse. But as that situation likely indicates you will be using external monitors, I hope that you will find some creative way to plug your mouse in as needed.Q: Is the sound quality good?A: Sadly, no. The sound on this laptop honestly just sucks in my subjective opinion. This opinion may stem from my being a musician on the side and I have pretty high expectations for sound quality. For a laptop this amazing in every other aspect, though, I am willing to make concessions. If you are gaming in public, you while likely be using headphones and if you are plugged in at home, Bluetooth and external speakers will solve this issue. This is not too big of a deal for me, especially since you get the trade off of having the awesome HiFi audio port. For a laptop this small and this light, there had to be compromises in some areas, and I think the speakers drew the short straw.Q: Does the panel on this laptop suck?A: No, that is the 001 from Best Buy that most people complain about. This has a quality full HD IPS panel that is not lacking in performance.Q: How is the battery life?A: In a word: Good! The battery in this laptop actually does a remarkable job of sipping rather than gulping the energy when you place it on eco mode with the Dragon Center app, power saver mode in Windows Power Management, and dim the screen down about halfway. On a average day of studying with near constant web browsing and lecture video viewing, I get about 4 to 5-1/2 hours of battery. During a heavy gaming session on battery alone, perhaps an hour and a half. There are million ways you can tune the power management on this laptop to suit your individual needs, so I wouldn't be stressed about it unless you are looking for ultrabook-like battery life-in which case, you are shopping in the wrong category of laptops.That is all I can think of for the moment, please feel free to comment at will and I will be happy to reply! Take care and good luck with your purchase!

review_title: Conflicted - great tablet with some issues
review_text: UPDATE 12/16/19: I contacted the seller through Amazon on 11 December. On 16 December I did receive an HP stylus in the mail, but as it is missing batteries I'm still not sure how well it works. The stylus I received also did not include any of the accessories, lanyard, spare tips, etc. that would normally come with this model.I purchased the model listed as "512GB SSD + Intel M7-6Y75" "HP Elite X2 1012 G1 Detachable 2-IN-1 Business Tablet Laptop 12 inches FHD IPS Touchscreen (1920x1280), Intel Core m7-6Y75, 512GB SSD, 8GB RAM, Keyboard + Pen, Windows 10 Pro (Renewed)"I ordered on 9 Dec 2019 and received the shipment as promised on 11 Dec 2019.The tablet was sent inside a plain brown box, and was wrapped in adequate amounts of bubble wrap. Shipment came via FedEx from MLG Ventures Inc in New Jersey. The package was sent with "Adult Signature Required" which I was not informed nor aware of until I got the text from FedEx Delivery Manager while at work the day of delivery! Luckily my oldest daughter was home from school that day and could sign.Although it is specifically listed in the description I did NOT receive a HP Active Pen/Stylus in the box. I will be contacting the seller and will update if remedied. (See update at top, I did receive a stylus after contacting the seller but it was missing battery and accessories)Physical Condition and Hardware:- The tablet itself looks to be in very good condition. Some minor smudges on screen and keyboard but no evidence of any physical damage or scratches other than a few nearly impossible to see nicks. The screen is perfect.- The USB C charger looks well loved. it is pretty beat and scratched up, but it does work. The fabric base of the detachable keyboard shows some obvious wear and tear, especially on the corners where it is worn smooth/shiny. There is also a small nick in the fabric in the hinge area. Nothing major, but not sure I'd say the charger and keyboard "*look like new*" like the amazon listing says.- According to HWMonitor, battery wear level is 0% (A good thing, though not always an accurate reflection of battery health this typically means the battery has had very few heavy charge cycles and has plenty of life left).- According to HP's Warranty website the system was sold new in April 2017. For some reason the BIOS reports the "born-on date" as March 2019 though. Perhaps the born-on date was reset during the refurb process, or a warranty replacement of the main board.- The system actually has an extended warranty HP Care Pack active through May 2020. Not sure if HP would honor for a second owner though.- The specific model I received is the HP Elite X2 1012 G1 Model 1GB07US#ABASome details not shown in the listing, this particular tablet has:Samsung 512GB SATA III 6Gb/s m2 slot (2280) SSD MZNLN512HMJP-000H1An Intel Dual Band Wireless 8260AC 2x2 WiFi Card+ Bluetooth 4.2 (non WiGig Version, so no wireless dock support)8GB of Hynix LPDDR3 1866 MHz dual channel RAM (2x4GB) (non-upgradeable as it is soldered to the main board)This model does not include a Fingerprint Reader, although it appears to have one on the rear it is just a blank cover and there is no reader module.The keyboard I received is the base model keyboard, not the version shown in the listing picture with an integrated Smart Card/NFC reader.There is no WWAN (4g / cell) radio and the sim slot is not even removableWindows and Drivers installation:- When first taken out of the box, the tablet would not turn on or even display lights. The battery was completely dead. After a brief moment of panic I plugged in the charger and let it charge for an hour before use. Once the battery had some juice it booted to the Windows "finish setup" screen in just a few seconds.- The tablet arrived with no drivers installed at all - just a plain stock install of Win 10 Pro. Luckily the default windows WiFi drivers were functioning.- Likely due to lack of appropriate drivers, the system also behaved erratically (would not wake from sleep, etc.) out of the box.- Once setup with correct drivers it appears to be stable. To get the drivers, I first downloaded the support assistant from HP support website, then selected which drivers to install. I know some people dislike manufacturer "bloat ware" but support assistant seems to be pretty light and unobtrusive, and can always be uninstalled once drivers are set up. The other option is to manually download and install the 13 missing drivers from a list of dozens of choices on the HP support website. Not ideal.Initial Impressions:I bought this tablet as a "companion" device to take when traveling for work when I also have to carry a work laptop, or vacation when I don't want to lug my big Alienware laptop around.After spending a few hours getting drivers set up and windows updates installed, I'm loving the form factor and build quality of this. The only real complaint I have is one that might be a deal breaker for me. The audio is absolutely horrible. I don't mean just the volume or quality, but both! It isn't really usable without headphones. I can barely hear the normal Windows system sounds (e.g. plugging in USB) without having my ear 6" from the speaker at max volume. Trying to watch movies or listen to music is basically pointless. I can't believe this thing has Bang and Olufsen's name on it.- The track pad and touch screen seem to work well. Will update about stylus if/when I receive it.- After a full charge, I was able to run about 5 hours while streaming video and still had 20% battery time remaining.Overall Value:As far as value goes, I'm not sure its worth the price I paid, especially considering this is a 3+ year old model. For a few dollars more you could get a brand new Surface Pro Go bundle with similar specs (albeit a smaller 10" screen). Because of that I'm rating this in the middle at 3 stars.

review_text: First, about me: PC enthusiast, (/r/PCMR shoutout) ive put together 4-5 different desktops in the past few years, building from scratch.  Ive also owned several pre-builts, including the infamous Alienware.  I've owned high-end desktops ( 7700k, 1080ti) and made budget-builds for a friend and my wife (Intel Pentium g4620).Now to the Lenovo Legion Y720 - the core components: I7-7700HQ at 2.8ghz (Kaby Lake, 4 core 8 thread), 16gb DDR4 @ 2400mhz, GTX 1060 6GB, and a 500gb NVME PCIE SSD (not sure make any model but I think it's a Samsung), the panel is a 1080p full hd IPS @ 60hz.Other features: It has a built in Xbox controller connection, so you don't have to buy the stupid dongle for 30$ (the dongle is horrifyingly large as well.)  It has a back lit keyboard, several different lighting patterns and options, built in camera & mic, some really high quality sound output (Dolby Atmos), and a thunderbolt.First impression out of the box - Looks very clean and nice. It's not a gigantic behemoth, it's a larger laptop but it doesn't look ridiculous like some of those you have probably seen that I would be embarrassed to pull out in a Starbucks.  Mostly matte black with some crimson detail work, really impressive.  Not gaudy. Keyboard has a nice key-feel to it, easy to type on and game with.  Another reviewer I read used the word "chiclet" that is a good word for the keys.  It has the normal stickers applied, I took mine off and it looks a lot cleaner.  (the intel, gtx, and the Lenovo sticker are all on the keyboard)After setup and windows update: I am  happy to report the bloatware and garbage preinstalled software is not that bad.  That evil plague "McCaffee" is present, unfortunately.  Just spend a few minutes turning off as much of that stuff as you can you'll end up with a relatively clean desktop.  The onboard Lenovo software is called Lenovo Nerve Sense - it allows you to setup and alter the keyboard colors and back light, has an "extreme cooling" profile to power up your fans, some sound features, and a network "priority" feature that purports to prioritize games being played for bandwidth purposes I presume.Gaming: The laptop is powered by a GTX 1060, which is an Upper-middle tier GPU and a good sweet spot for 1080p gaming.  Honestly, this is as good of a card (especially 6gb model) you will ever need for this panel.  You will be able to run any game you want, maxed out, and at 60fps.  Sorry console gamers :( You can't do that.  I've been playing Victor Vran ( A steam ARPG) and Bioshock, both run beautifully.  It's pretty impressive how much power you can get into such a small box.  You also has a i7 CPU, it's not a 7700k, but you are still getting extra cores and the delicious multi threading you need.  Some of the newer games are starting to care more about the CPU you are running, so this is a good spot to be in.  You used to recommend staying in the i5 area (for budget purposes) because you didnt get much bang from an i7 for gaming - that is becoming less true year after year.Conclusion and overall thoughts and Misc.:Overall, im giving it a 4 star based really only on a price to performance analysis.  If this was being sold at 1100$ It would be an easy 5 star.  The GPU alone runs about $300.  The key point to remember is this is a LAPTOP.  Laptops will always be more expensive than a proportionally powerful desktop BUT you get 4 things you have to remember to factor in, MOBILITY, SIZE, and a built in Keyboard and Monitor.  So Yes, you can build a desktop that has similar specs as this for maybe a grand, but you wont get a monitor or a keyboard and it wont be mobile.  Point being, when you consider the full package - the price makes sense.....at some point.  For $1500? It's worth it but it isn't a bargain.  If you can find this laptop for anything less than $1400.  It would be a really easy buy.  All in all, a really sweet looking (but not gaudy) laptop with a large blazing fast SSD, a great GPU, fast future-proof i7 CPU and a nice keyboard/monitor setup.  If you're in the market for a gaming laptop and you care about price to performance, this fits the bill.  In terms of the competition, the Acer Helios is the only one that (just because of the price) is competitive.  This Legion model has a lot of perks that put it above the Helios (thunderbolt, larger faster SSD, better cooling, built in bluetooth for the xbox controller) but it will cost you a few hundred bucks extra.  Lenovo Legion has a really nice, higher-end gaming laptop that should be very competitive in this market.  There are a lot out there trying to rip you off for sub-par hardware, this aint that.  It's good performance for a fair price, my only complaint is as stated above, is that this needs to sell for like 1200-1400 then it would be the #1 king.

review_title: great laptop but has quality issues
review_text: I bought this laptop about a month ago and am very pleased.  My needs are not very demanding but there are times when I need the power of a game PC.  The desktop graphics are smooth and without hesitation.  The machine has more than enough power to attach an HDMI TV, extend the desktop to it and watch a DVD on one while using the other half for other things.  The fans in my other non-gaming laptops would be roaring to keep them cool before eventually overheating.  This Asus, however, doesn't break a sweat.  It's very quiet even when the CPU is stressed.  I've played a few games, and the graphics are incredibly smooth, and the machine is very responsive to the keyboard and game controllers.When editing photos and videos, it handles the large volumes of image data like a champ.It crunches through large computational Excel spreadsheets in a fraction of the time as my 8 year old Dell Vostro 1700.There are a few minor quirks.  The touchpad is very large.  Small hands will have trouble typing without accidentally touching it.  My adult hands are of average size, but they still sometimes accidentally touch it, and this causes the cursor and focus to unexpectedly jump elsewhere.  The numlock doesn't stay when the PC is shutdown. It will stay when hibernated.  The red on black keyboard lettering is not easily visible, even when the keyboard is back light is on.  I would have preferred the usual white on black lettering.  Occasionally, when the screen blanks to conserve power it can't be reactivated despite the machine being awake.  One work-around is to press fn-F1 which hibernates the machine and then immediately awaken it by pressing any key.  There don't seem to be any side-effects.Compared to my old Dell Vostro 1700, also a 17" screen, the Asus is an inch larger in width and length and will not fit inside my backpack which itself is large.  The power adapter is also quite large and heavy.  The laptop and power adapter combined must weight about 13 pounds.It's a solid laptop.  The only thing more that I could ask for is a 4K display.4/1/18 - updateAfter owning this laptop about a year, I'm downgrading the rating to 3 stars.  Perhaps I got a lemon, but the laptop has been sent to Asus 3 times for servicing.  The first time was to fix a power-on issue, where it would not power-on or its display would be remain black.  It would also lose WiFi connection after a couple hours.  It was with Asus for almost a month while parts were ordered.  The second time was to fix the same power-on issue and replace the optical drive because it would not write on DVD+R DL media.  The third time (currently) is to fix the num-lock indicator light which stopped working after the second repair.  Additionally, the laptop case was damaged upon arrival at Asus, so it took a couple days to resolve this too.  It has been two weeks, and I hope it will be returned to me this week.

review_title: UPDATED - AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE (Was "Great mobo, screen, and keyboard.  *BULGING* battery and *AWFUL* warranty.")
review_text: UPDATE - 2018/10/15 - Reducing from 2 stars to 1 star.----------------------The batteries I'd ordered to replace the bulging one turned out to be the wrong size / type.  Additionally, when trying to acquire the correct battery (BTY-M6K - for this exact model - the other GS63VRs take a different one ... which I now have 2 of) since then, I've had even worse luck getting ahold of them.  The laptop is still without battery and, given that the battery supports the keyboard, it doesn't seem safe to use it in a stationary deployment even.  In short, this rather expensive laptop has been sitting dead on my desk since July, after only working for a little over 6 months before that.The lesson seems to be AVOID MSI LIKE THE PLAGUE.  If you have issues, odds are you will not only have no warranty support (as they (on some products, at least) write the period as starting at date of manufacture) nor will you be able to acquire parts to affect repairs outside of them either.Original review (2 stars)----------------------In terms of bulk, keyboard feel, and overall performance, this is a great little unit.  My main problem is that, after just shy of 6 months of use, the battery pack had swollen enough to warp the chassis enough that the touchpad is sticking out on one side and the spacebar of the keyboard is becoming flakey.  The bulge is sufficient that I don't want to close it for fear of damage to the screen, as the area where one's left hand rests while typing is now about 2mm thicker than it should be, if not more.What compounds the issue, and has me borderline livid, is that the warranty is written as one year FROM DATE OF MANUFACTURE and, as my unit was built in the spring of of 2017, it's now out of warranty, despite my having only purchased it at the end of 2017 and started use right before the end of the year.  So, I give congratulations to the people who did the board design, and those who chose the keyboard, screen, etc... and did overall mechanical work on it.  I give hatred and loathing to the business people at MSi and whoever specified, or tested, these batteries.Also, be aware, sourcing a new battery for these isn't that easy.  It's taken me weeks to find some that were actually in stock anywhere in the world.  I ordered two, just in case.The bulge is quite visible in the attached photo.  That's not distortion or perspective you're seeing.

I have heard that the keyboard covers that can be purchased for this model spread the light out a bit and make the backlighting look great.---CPU: Although it is an i3, this 7th gen CPU is more than capable of handling multiple demanding apps and light gaming (you won't be running any AAA graphically demanding titles on it, but light/moderate gaming and older titles should prove playable). There is little heat generated from this CPU while browsing the web or watching videos.---Screen: I prefer larger screens. The laptop I use for work is a Lenovo X240 with a 13" screen and 1280x768 resolution which looks terrible in comparison to this screen. Full 1080p HD resolution looks good on the larger 15.6" screen and the brightness is spot on. I am currently in a well lit room (no direct light on the monitor) and I have the brightness set all the way down and it is a very comfortable view while typing this review. I noticed that the viewing angles are fairly good when looking at the screen from the sides but not so much from above/below.---Ports: This thing has all the ports you'll need! USB 3.1 Type-C port is a huge bonus in making this machine future compatible with phones/monitors/etc. There are also 2 other USB 3.1 Type-A ports that boast super fast data transfer. The HDMI and VGA ports are great, although I think it is about time to kill off the VGA port.---Upgradability: You'll eventually want to add some RAM (at least 4GB) and this machine makes it easy to do just that. I haven't upgraded yet, still running fine on 4GB but will be purchasing an 8GB module soon for a total of 12GB. I'm not much of a multitasker and usually don't burn through RAM as much as the next guy, but I recognize that 4GB is pretty much the bare minimum nowadays. There is an M.2 SSD slot that is open and ready for a super speedy SSD (will be purchasing next week). This means that you can upgrade your system to run on an SSD without having to remove the 2.5" SATA HDD (which is a generous 1TB). You can also upgrade to a SATA SSD if you wish, but I believe you'll be happier going the M.2 route.CON:---HDD: The hard drive is 5400rpm and very slow. Boot times are around 1.5-2 minutes and reading large data sets is gonna take some time. This is the main reason I'll be updating to an M.2 SSD.---Trackpad: By far one of the touchiest track pads I have ever dealt with. I constantly am having to disable it by pressing Fn+F7 while typing. It does have a nice click to it but the cursor moves very erratically sometimes and I would recommend using a Bluetooth/USB mouse.---Speaker: Use headphones...that's all I'm going to say.So...even though I have a few things I dislike about the laptop, you need to look at the price. You are getting a lot of laptop for the low price of $350 and if you are just looking to do basic things and aren't into heavy gaming or video editing, this laptop may just be perfect for you.

review_title: Linux performance rivals that of my last gen Ryzen desktop
review_text: Removed Windows as soon as I received my laptop, and installed Linux Mint Ulyana with Cinnamon Desktop. Only issue was with display resolution and HDMI output. The 4000 series processor requires a newer kernel which can easily be installed via Update Manager -> View -> Linux Kernels. Everything seems to be working with the 5.8.0-29 kernel with the exception of Bluetooth which is a bit buggy, but usable. With 8 cores, performance is comparable or better than my last gen Ryzen 5 desktop computer depending on usage. Heating is not an issue with general usage, but it will warm up if you begin pushing those cores. For my usage, (no gaming) CPU temps always stayed below 70C, and were below 50C most of the time. No overheating issues as long as you keep the fan intake on the bottom clear of obstructions. The bios on this laptop is very limited, no overclocking or tuning is possible. Display brightness is acceptable, not the best in direct sunlight. There is some shadowing when viewed at an angle. Memory and storage upgrades require removal of the entire bottom cover which took some time to perform. Keyboard backlight is helpful in low light conditions. Yes, the letters themselves light up, not just the border. This is a respectable developers laptop, and a very decent general purpose laptop.

review_title: it's not a bad laptop overall
review_text: I've had this laptop for about two weeks now. Having played around with it a bit and configured Windows 10 to what I want, it's not a bad laptop overall. It's not too heavy for me, seems well built and solid enough, and battery life, so far, has been running about 6-7 hours. I've had it on my lap for an hour or more at a time and it never gets beyond warm. Hard drive speed with the SSD (my first time using one) is fast, but I haven't really had to put the machine to work in order to detect just how much faster it is than a regular hard drive.The screen and keyboard are adequate (the keypad is a welcome for me as well). The key response is just enough to give you the feel that you've pressed the button; there is a light noiseless click when depressing keys, which I like. As to no keyboard backlighting, I don't care; I need an external source of light when I type, so I'm not bothered by that missing feature.The touchpad is apparently not an ELAN, so you can't run the Precision software Microsoft puts out for that, which I would rather use than the ASUS Gestures - it's not as fine-tuning as it should be, but it works.Battery Health Charger (software that enables better battery longevity) does not come with this laptop, and the software (which is downloadable) will not work when installed after the fact. This confirmed by ASUS after I couldn't get it to work.As for graphics, you cannot disable the integrated Intel graphics processor (HD 620, I believe it is) in order to just run the NVIDIA 940 - bios options do not support this option, and disabling the Intel driver in the Device Manager disables both drivers. Thus, it seems the only way to kick in the NVIDIA driver is to use its control panel to set it to run with the particular software you wish, if you can find it listed and available to do so. Otherwise, the Intel on-board is a good processor and will do just fine for general all-around graphics processing, which is all I need.By the way, it is because of the touchpad, battery and graphics shortcomings I've noted above that I've given the laptop 4 instead of 5 stars.As to wifi, download speeds, this, that and the other related features, I've paid little attention to those matters because it's not that important for me. I will be using this machine pretty much just for Internet research, writing, some YouTube and other minor program running. (This machine will be taking over for my desktop, which I will upgrade and use for what few games I play, for photography post processing and for composing music - much bigger and nicer monitor on the desktop!)The problems that I've come across have been Windows issues, I'm sure (confirmed after doing some research on the Net): battery icon disappears and the speaker icon doesn't do anything when clicking on it. At the moment, both, however, are working. For the battery, the fix was to uninstall the battery drivers in Device Manager and rescan the hardware (one driver at a time). For the speakers, it's a matter of either using the fn-F11/12 keys (volume control) or restarting Windows Explorer through the Task Manager. Both fixes, I don't believe, are machine related, and I'm still testing these "fixes" to see if the battery and speaker icons will stay fixed. (Doing so as I write.)So overall, I'm quite pleased with the machine. I tried to find a lower performance machine for a few hundred dollars cheaper that got equally good reviews as this one but simply couldn't find what made me feel comfortable in the purchase. So, I dropped a grand on this one. It's got to last me a good 5-7 years, I hope, to make the investment well worth it. We will see.

review_title: Very powerful laptop at a great price
review_text: This laptop is a very powerful machine and a great value for all of the hardware features.Pros:powerful quad core amd 2.7 GHZ 2017 CPU with turbo boost up to 3.6 GHZ8 Gig DDR4 ram, expandable to 16 gig ddr4 ram1 TB hard driveUSB Type-C (future proof your household)2 USB 3.01 HDMIWebcamDVD-RW DriveBluetoothAC wifi (future proof your household)Thin and sturdy constructionRadeon R7 GPUCons:I have read that some folks expected a brighter screenBattery lasts a couple of hours of regular useI researched all of the specifications of this laptop, and I just was not able to get these awesome hardware specs without spending over $500.  I was looking for at least a quad-core cpu, and at least 4 gigs of DDR4 ram.  Usually laptops with 8 gigs of DDR4 ram are well over $500.  Many budget laptops today still have DDR3 ram, and usually have 4 gigs of DDR3 ram.  We might as well future proof our experience with USB Type-C, and AC wifi so our purchase isn't outdated for a couple of years at least.  The 1 Terra-byte hard drive is more than enough space for a lifetime, but is also what is holding this laptop back.  I went ahead and purchased an external HDD enclosure, and a Samsung evo 850 500 GB solid state hard drive.  I transferred my data to the Samsung SSD, installed the SSD into the laptop, and reused the 1 terra-byte HDD which came in the laptop as an external 1 TB drive.  This laptop completely starts and is all ready to be used in aproximately 2-3 seconds after pressing the ON button with the solid state drive.  With the solid state drive, this machine is really comparable to other laptops which cost $800 and above.  I have had my laptop only for about a month, and I love it so far!  I am a student, and I primarily use my laptop for research and homework at school, but I also play some games on it too.  I immediately purchased a soft neoprene case for this laptop, and put the laptop in the neoprene case, which goes into my padded backpack laptop pocket to protect my investment.  This laptop is so powerful with awesome hardware that I thought about purchasing 2 of them because it's a steal.  I'll report back in the future if I run into any issues, but I am extremely happy with my future proof and powerful laptop at this price!

I do have to make sure there are no apps running in the background or the game will crash. I think this is because of the fact that this device does not have a dedicated graphics card. So the laptop, by default, is trying to run the game and other programs. Therefore it crashes. It crashing is not a huge deal to me....as long as I can play the game.However, the device itself is soooo slow. It takes forever to boot up and it takes forever to perform a Windows action such as opening control panel, settings, right clicking, file explorer, ect.The battery life is INFURIATING!! It absolutely has to stay plugged in or else it will die within an 45 min to a hour of use. And for a battery life that is as abysmal as it is, the darn laptop cable is only an inch long. So thanks Lenovo for giving me a nonexsistent battery coupled with this short cord that is as long as my hangnail.Also, if you are working in an environment with alot of natural light or direct sunlight, good luck being able to see the screen. The screen brightness is a joke. If im sitting right next to a window, I cant see the screen.So is this laptop worth $460? Goodness no! This is easily a $300 laptop. My $250 chromebook is much better than this. The only thing this device does decently is run my Sims game.  If Chromebooks came with enough storage, RAM, CPU and GPU to run the computer games, I wouldnt have bought this overpriced laptop.
