review_title: Only buy if this is absolutely, without a doubt, your last choice
review_text: This is absolutely the worst computer you could ever throw your money at. That being said, yes, this is my personal opinion based on my experiences. However, I'll break down for you why I think so.I bought this computer after my three-year old MacBook Pro (2012 model) died on me (also a horrid computer after just a year or two of use). I was going abroad for a semester and needed a computer that was quick, efficient, and cheap. This computer guaranteed that with its super fast wifi antennas, <$250 price tag, and a bunch of other empty promises. I use my computer for schoolwork (researching, typing up essays, making presentations) and a bit of leisure (social media, occasional video and game streaming). All in all, I use my computer for about 3-5 hours of every day. It used to be more but this computer has made even these 3-5 hours of use difficult.Before I even start going into problems, keep in mind I have not even had this computer for 6 months. I got it at the end of December and it's early May now.This computer began giving me problems from day one. I knew it would be slow before removing all the bloatware but even then, it was almost impossible. Its tiny 32GB EMMC came practically full and after removing all I could, I was still at about 22/29GB. I also have an issue with the fact that this computer runs on EMMC instead of HDD; for those of you who don't know what the difference is: tablets/phones tend to run on EMMC while other computers run on either HDD, SSD, or HDD and SSD. Anyways, this computer is NOT convertible (meaning it does not turn into a tablet) NOR touchscreen so I don't see the need for EMMC over HDD (my guess is it keeps the price cheap). However, it sucks. It makes the computer run slower regardless of if you're in desktop mode or (the mostly pointless) tablet mode.The first time I turned it on, it worked alright. Slow, but alright. The second day I used it, it turned on but did not boot. My cursor would appear after the HP symbol but instead of taking me to the sign in page, it would just stay on a blank screen. Forcing the computer off and then back on seemed to fix the issue (after disk checking) but was still a bit of a damper in my mood. This still happens occasionally but it's the least of my worries at this point, honestly.I have not been able to update this computer since day 1 either. I try to download all of my apps on my OneDrive so I don't take up storage but even then, it's impossible. The new update is requiring a whopping THIRTEEN and a half GB of space to download. I have less than 1GB available and I believe I've only downloaded three or four applications to the actual EMMC that were all around or less than 1 GB of space.It runs slower than anything I've ever seen. I honestly think my 1998 Windows could've opened a web page faster. It's taken this computer up to 10 minutes to open Chrome right after start-up. It's also more moody than anything I've ever seen. Sometimes it will work so slow that you can't even move the mouse in time. The first time it happened, I spent the better part of a half hour just trying to get the menu bar to open so I could click shut down. Nowadays I'm too impatient (and frustrated) to wait and just shut it off manually.Randomly, a month or two ago, it began displaying a random picture I had saved/created on my OneDrive as my lock screen background. Yet, when I go into the settings, it says it's still set to what it should be. Usually going into settings fixes it but its just another little annoyance. Recently, it's also picked up this habit of not displaying anything on start-up. The power light will be on but the screen will remain black. I don't know how to fix it besides just giving it time (and I mean hours, usually overnight, of it being off) because even turning it on and off doesn't work. It's happened to me twice so far and as a college student approaching finals I REALLY don't appreciate it one bit.Lastly, the only pro for me about this computer is the weight. It definitely is lightweight and much better to carry than my old macbook pro. But what good is that if it doesn't do what I need it to when I need it?Synopsis/tldr; Unless you desperately need a computer and really can't afford anything over this price, then I guess you're stuck. But if you have the space to save for something better, please do. I can assure you a much better laptop is out there within the $300-$700 range. While it may not be perfect, it can get you through much more than this. This laptop is incredibly slow by nature, barely has space, and is littered with bugs and issues. It is, at best, a minimally functioning computer.

I waited a week before writing this review.  I wanted to get a better feel on the laptop first before giving my thoughts.I want to first say that when it arrived it came pre-loaded with Windows 10 Pro but no activation key.  I communicated with Amazon Customer Support and they took care of the issue with no problem.AUDIONow, what I found is that the audio wi not rock a party for you at all, lol!  It is not overwhelming by any stretch of the imagination.  However it is adequate and on full volume you can hear decently enough.RUNS HOTThis machines run hot so if you game or video edit then be prepared to by some cooling accessories.  I got a laptop cooler and 2 vacuum coolers for my machine to help with cooling.  I downloaded the AMD Ryzen Master application to monitor the CPU temp.  It was running around 89 to 90 degrees Celcius while rendering video before the the cooling units.  I will update later to give more information on how well the cooling units help.  Be aware if you buy a laptop cooling pad that you should get one with the fan in the center to match the position of the irrigation holes for cool air in on the bottom of this laptop.  I used duct tape to fill the gaps from the fan duct to the cooling bars (See Images Below).  I saw on a YouTube video where a guy recommended this.  It made sense to me.  If the air from the fan is to move across the cooling bars then you probably do not want that hot air to be able to circulate back into the inside of the laptop enclosure.  I want it all to exhaust.  It is a beast of a machine and that is why I bought it.  I wish ASUS would have done a better job with cooling though.  I guess it would cost more if they did.  So there is a trade off.HDD - Comes with a 256GB M.2 SSD drive and a slow 1TB 5200 RPM secondary drive.  If you are planing to use this machine to edit 4K video you will need to upgrade the secondary drive to a SSD.  The 1TB drive bottle necks the editing process.TOUCHPADWhen I got it the touch pad was garbage.  Very inconsistent and unreliable.  Nothing like being engulfed into an editing project and the touchpad begins to do what wants...  That SUCKS!SOLUTION: I found on a forum a guy having the same issue and he recommended a driver (Smart Gesture Windows 10) that can be downloaded on Asus website.  I installed it and it is actually working a lot better.  Has a interface in Control Panel where you can fine tune a few things.ADOBE CC SUITE ABILITYIf you are planning to edit 4K video with this machine you will have to upgrade RAM to 32GB.  I found the same exact 16GB Samsung DDR4 chip on Amazon for $199.  There are two slots so this helped me out tremendously.  Especially with After Effects CC 2018 because that program is a RESOURCE HOG!  Had problems loading previous projects and saving projects before upgrading in AE CC 2018.GPUGPU Works really well.  Make sure you update the driver for the GPU.  Comes with Radeon RX580 and the driver that was pre-installed was a older version than the current one out.  Once I updated the driver I got better performance with After Effects CC 2018.POWER BRICKIt is huge but that does not bother me at all.  This machine needs adequate power to deliver the performance I wanted so no issue with me what so ever.I bought the laptop to edit my projects on the go away from home.  To be honest this machine is as beefy as my desktop.  What an awesome performing PC.  The AMD is high ranking for the price point and you can not get the same resources anywhere currently at this price point in a new machine.  The benchmarks speak for themselves.  This machine does not have a CD combo drive at all but that does not bother me either.  It has enough connectivity to get the job done.EDIT (4/20/2018): I got the fans that I mentioned above.  I'm getting about 20 degrees Celsius less while editing than I was getting before.  It is definitely worth protecting my $1.5K investment for longevity.

review_title: It's a Great Laptop: Even Novices Like Myself Can Upgrade it (Explained)
review_text: It's a Great Laptop: Even Novices Like Myself Can Upgrade it (Explained)I came into this laptop for the same reason most of you probably are; my budget is "as cheap as I can make it" while still having a functional Windows operating system (not a chromebook) for school related reasons. 350 dollars will buy you a keyboard with a number pad, a full 1080p display, 3 usbs, an hdmi output, and so on. The charging unit is L shaped which for the uninitiated, is a really good thing. Charging cords that are straight will stick straight out of your laptop which make them incredibly easy to catch onto a surface or bump with your hand which can damage the laptop or the cord, whereas L shaped chargers curve in to help prevent accidental tugs. It seems like a silly thing to talk about but you'd be surprised, especially with lower-end laptops, how problematic that can be when it isn't L shaped (for that reason, I recommend staying away from Dell Inspirons and any other laptop like that).For 350 dollars, the main value is in the display and for some, the full backbit keyboard which includes a number pad. This unit, of course, comes with a slow 1 tb HDD for storage which, while slow, is going to be far more than most users will need even if they're downloading some games and HD movies. The 4 gigs of ram is serviceable. Some of you may wish to upgrade this computer but aren't confident in your abilities so I'm here to say, it's very simple and if I can do it, you can do it. So let's get into it.Upgrading the unit is very simple and if you search on youtube, you'll find guides that show it.Otherwise, I've tried to lay it out in my photos. On the back-end, there's a large panel attached by 3 screws towards the front which you remove. I show in the photos where to place your finger under to peal the panel off. It'll reveal the 4 gigs of RAM they've given you, an empty slot for you to upgrade, and what is called an M.2 slot. The M.2 slot is where you can install a second storage device in addition to the 1 tb of slow hdd that the computer comes with, and you'd be installing a fast SSD. These are empty slots so all you have to do is plug these things in, and you're good to go.Kingston Technology HyperX Impact 8GB 2133MHz DDR4 CL13 SODIMM Laptop Memory HX421S13IB/8 is the RAM I used to upgrade with. An additional 4 gigs should serve you well and will offer something called duel boot, which is what happens when you have two sticks of ram of the same size. If you were so inclined, you could pay for 8 gigs of ram to bring you to twelve, or buy two sticks of 4/8/16 and replace the stick they give you as the laptop can theoretically be taken up to 32. But don't do that, honestly keep it simple and just buy an extra 4 gigs to bring yourself up to 8, or maybe 8 to bring yourself to 12 if you see yourself running many programs at once or are the type to have 50 tabs open. It's important to match the MHz speed of 2133 and that card will do it. Anyways, you just buy the 4 or 8 gig card, plug it in as shown until it clicks in (see the video for more help) and you're done. If you go into your computer information, you'll see that you have more ram and you'll be able to feel the difference. One final tip, if you aren't in a rush, wait for something like cyber monday to get great deals.Installing an ssd and moving your copy of windows onto it will be a world of difference in boot times. There are drives out there sized 128gb which can hold windows and that'll get the job done for you, otherwise if you're installing a lot of programs or games, you can buy 256gb, 500gb, they go up to 2 tb now which is insane. Again use your judgement for what you want, if you aren't going to install large programs or games then a small one will suffice. Crucial MX300 275GB M.2 (2280) Internal Solid State Drive - CT275MX300SSD4 is what I went with, which is 256gb. I show how to install it in the pictures and youtube videos show it well. One thing I should stress is that as shown in my picture, you place it on the bolt where it should fit and then attach the screw over it. You may have to initialize the drive before you see and use it on your computer. After that, it's a good idea to install all programs on that ssd drive and use your 1tb hdd for all your miscellaneous storage. It's a bit of a process to move your copy of windows onto your ssd but a worthwhile one.You can also upgrade the 1tb hhd but that seems excessive, and it can screw up the m.2. In summary, when it comes to upgrading, upgrading the ram should be your pick if you only do one as it's cheap and will make a huge impact. Adding on an ssd is also simple. If you move windows and programs onto the ssd, and you upgrade your ram, you'll have a real real nice laptop and it shouldn't cost you more than 500 total. This laptop's integrated graphics will limit it when it comes to playing modern, intensive games but the 7th generation i3 hold up strong and upgrading ram/ssd will improve that.So hopefully this clears up some of the confusion when it comes to upgrading. This is a great budget laptop and it's served me well for school. I'm a total novice when it comes to dealing with computer hardware and had to do a lot of reading to figure out how to upgrade this thing. The only real downside to this laptop, which is to be expected in the pricerange, is the integrated graphics card which limits its gaming possibilities but in reality, it makes much more sense to have a basic laptop and a dedicated gaming pc at home as you'll get much more bang for your buck that way. I'm amazed by how much 350 can get you these days and can only dream about what laptop value shopping will be like 10 years from now. I strongly urge you to purchase this unit, even if you're not going to screw around with upgrades, over spending the $1,500 Apple wants for their worst 13 inch laptop (they want 2,400 for their low-end 15 inch laptop.) Pocket the money and you could build yourself a fantastic gaming PC, or take the wife out to a nice meal, several meals, or invest in your 401k. Buying expensive laptops is a luxury with minimal value and you'd be better off spending it on other luxuries instead, as this is a new golden standard for laptops.

review_title: So far so good.  A lot of laptop for the price, but some technical quirks mean you need to research it a bit first.
review_text: This is just  "First Impressions" review, as I just got the laptop yesterday.  That said, I will speak at length about the value of this computer.As with any new Windows 10 installation, the Acer required quite a bit of time before it was ready for use.  After answering a few questions (pay special attention to the security and privacy options), I had to wait for a slew of updates.  While not unexpected, during this process the laptop was essentially unusable.  After many updates and about six restarts over the course of a couple hours, it was good to go.One of the first things I noticed about the way it ran was the fact that was at or near 100% HD utilization much of the time.  That means it was constantly accessing the HD.  This, by the way, was after the updates were done.  Part of this was due to Windows indexing the drive, part was due to the fact that Windows 10 isn't always great at dynamically creating the Virtual RAM swap space.  After I changed it (4096 minimum, 8192 maximum) in the Advanced System Settings, it started working quite smoothly.  I've ordered another stick of RAM to double what it already has, so that will also help.While waiting for the updates, I checked it out physically.  The screen, at the very top edge, has a seam between the front and back panel.  That seam is almost big enough to get a fingernail in there, and it's sharp enough to scrape me when I run my hand across it.  That's a bit concerning, but not at all different from my last mid-price laptop (an HP DV6 from about four years ago).  It speaks to the fit and finish of the unit, though, and I'm concerned that it will eventually turn from a seam into a gap.  The last thing I want to have to do is tape my new laptop.Also, I noticed the USB port on the right side of the unit will shock me if I touch it.  That's an issue I've seen on phones and laptops before.  Often, this is due to a short, but sometimes it's just the way the port was designed.  I don't like that, and will be examining it further.The trackpad is one of those that doesn't have separate buttons, but instead allows you to push it in to "left click".  It also has the areas on the bottom of the trackpad for left-button and right-button operations.  While it works quite well, I prefer having separate buttons.  Of course, I knew by the pictures that this would be the case, so it's not a surprise.The keyboard is fine.  It's backlit in a way, but the backlighting seems a little bit like an afterthought.  The backlighting does time-out if you're not using the keyboard for a minute or so.  Be prepared for that, as the backlight will come back on the moment you start typing again.While I planned on installing an SSD in the M.2 slot, I noticed that (like others) the slot didn't come with a standoff and a screw to hold the SSD drive in place.  There is a little plastic cover over the chip that's underneath the slot, and the screw-holes are present in the motherboard, so it's likely that the motherboard manufacturer anticipated the slot to be used.  That said, without the screw and the standoff, Acer seems to be saying they'd rather not have us use it.  Once I can find the screw type (looks like an M2.5x4mm with a .45mm pitch), I'll likely grab what I need and order an SSD.The memory is, according to Acer's own comments, supposed to be a DDR4 2133.  It's not.  It's a Kingston DDR4 2400.  As such, if I were you and I were thinking about adding another stick, I'd wait until I saw the memory it came with.  It's really easy to see - it's printed on a sticker on the RAM.  If you're not sure how to check it, jump on YouTube - there are a few videos showing people installing additional RAM.  Why is this important?  When adding RAM, while it's not necessary to get the same size and speed of RAM, it's actually really helpful.  Two 4GB sticks of the same type will function more efficiently than one 8GB stick, due to the multichannel nature of the chipset.  That only works if both sticks are functionally the same.  Yes, that includes speed.  No, that doesn't mean you have to get the same brand.This leads me to my last point:  Be aware of "cost creep".  If you buy this at $349, spend another $24 on RAM and spend $79 on a 240MB SSD drive, you might be teetering close to the next level of laptop.  Acer has a similar model with a seventh-gen i5-7200u, 8GB, and a 256GB SSD for $549 right now.  That's $200 more, with a faster CPU, the same 8GB you want, the same SSD you want, and it also comes with a moderately better GPU for games (NVidia 940MX).  Compare that, at $549 (or its competition) vs this one at $452.  The difference isn't so big, is it?  Yes, this one would still have the 1 TB 2.5" HD in it, so it's not an apples-to-apples comparison, but it's something you might want to consider.One more thing, before I forget:  The battery is not removable.  You'd have to crack open the case and likely void the warranty to remove it.Even with all that, if you're looking for a laptop that's short on price and long on features, this is likely a smart pick.  The adage of "You get what you pay for" still applies, but we're now getting a lot more than ever before for this price.

review_text: I've been using this for about a week now and so far it's great. While it's technically not a gaming laptop it will handle most newer games at medium to high settings with decent frame rates. The screen has great color and brightness, sound despite bottom facing speakers was louder than expected. The track-pad is responsive and snappy (no physical buttons) which might be a con to some. Battery life while watching netflix and surfing the web has been anywhere from 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 hours for me. I'm sure I could get more with some tweaking.I did have to order a mounting bracket and cable from Acer to attach my hdd (part # 42.GP4N2.SV1) that you can order from the Acer website for $8 usd. Other reviews have mentioned you can call them and see if they'll send you one for free. I opted to forgo the hassle and pay the 8 bucks.Pros: A lot of power packed into a $600 laptop. If you're not a hardcore gamer but still like to play games this might work for you. It exceeded my expectations.Cons: (These are nit picky and subjective)1. No cd drive but who uses those anymore anyway. If you do need one you can always plug a cheap usb one into it.2. If you want to add a 2.5 hdd for storage you need to order the cable and bracket along with being comfortable opening up a brand new laptop. The Acer website has a guide with pictures on how to do it, though.3. Plastic lid and aluminum palm rest show prints fairly easily. If you have ocd like me that might bother you but pretty minor.Over all very pleased with this purchase. You'd be hard pressed to find a laptop with 256g ssd, discrete graphics, i5 8250u processor and ddr4 memory for the money. (At the time of this review) Will update this in the future should my opinion change.

Update 7-2-2017:Been super pleased with this laptop.  Its so portable, I take it everywhere.  Earlier in my review I noted that the mouse kept disconnecting and that it was the dongle. From on my laptop to setting on my desk.  The keyboard overall is relatively cool, and the trackpad is actually rather cool.  Ive had trackpads so hot you can't touch them in days gone by, but this one is not so.The bottom of the laptop on the right side gets what I would call hot. I ordered another brand USB C dongle that is supposed to have shielding to prevent this, we will see how that goes.If I want to carry a usb hub or extension around in addition to the dongle thats ok, and its fine at my desk, but my keyboard and mouse are small and I travel with them, because in hotels and around in general - if I am sitting for any length of time- I can type faster and more ergonomically. Given Asus wants nearly $80 for this dongle, I would have expected that element to be better.The $28 dongle herehttps://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01GKSPMCQ/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1along with usb hubhttps://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00XMD7KPU/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1seems to work fine with this laptop. TL;DR : Received two essentially DOA laptops with different issues each. Could be a very nice machine, but I'm scared off of HP for good.For the sleek presentation and impressive hardware, the Omen X just didn't work for me. Not in a personal way, it just actually wouldn't work. When I purchased the laptop, it arrived with most of the lights (external/lid LEDs, power indicator, rear bar LEDs, OMEN LEDs on inside) not working, and a pressure mark on the LCD display. For having it be a brand new gaming laptop, I found this a little off-putting and concerning. Thankfully, Amazon was extremely responsive and sent me a replacement that same night. I chalked it up to it getting tossed around in shipping and hoped for a better replacement.The second unit that I received came out of the box with the fans just about screaming. I thought it might have been due to it being new and installing Windows updates, which there were plenty of. After letting updates install, I turned off the computer and waited the next day to test it out. After confirming that I had downloaded all available Windows and NVIDIA updates, I tried starting up a Vive. It was here where I noticed that something was seriously wrong. I ran the Steam VR test, and was told that I had an incompatible video card (see picture), and was skipping frames constantly. At this point, I opened up HP's own OMEN Command Center and noticed that the CPU was running extremely hot. I downloaded SpeedFan to verify if these readings were accurate, and confirmed they were. I tried contacting HP to see if they had any ideas for fixes, and was told it was a driver issue. After a support agent downloaded drivers from HP, the OMEN Command Center button on the keyboard no longer functioned, and the taskbar icon was broken as well. I was told by the HP agent that after installing the new set of drivers, I needed to wait 30 minutes to start using the laptop again. There was no sense of concern at all for the temperature readings they were seeing. I decided to wait an hour after shutdown, and the computer returned to excessive heats under no load. One of the fans, I noticed, appeared to not even be functioning with a reading of 126 RPM (see pictures).For $200, I would have maybe expected as much and told myself I got what I paid for. But at this price point, to have so many things go wrong, just seems like unbelievably bad luck or just poor quality. If you're purchasing this laptop, make sure everything works as intended and be grateful for Amazon's incredible customer support. As for HP, all I can say is that I'm disappointed.I can't, with a clean conscience, recommend this laptop.

Lenovo Ideapad 710s - Very smart looking, slim, lightweight laptop in an alloy case. I got the model with the I7-7500u processor, the Iris 620 GPU, 8GB memory and a 512 Solid state drive (model 80VQ003FUS) . This combination of processor and SSD provides for a very responsive laptop. I now use this laptop for running my stock analysis programs instead of my desktop PC because of the better processing speed. The sound from the speakers is better than many other laptops I've owned in the past.  The speakers are JBL, mounted on the base just below the screen that provide for very rich audio.Things I like:  1.) The screen/lid opens to 180 degree so you can get just the right angle when slouching on the couch ( and you don't need to worry about breaking the hinges ).  3.) The USB port on the right side always has power even when the computer is off, making it useful for charging a cell phone.  3.) The keyboard back light is adjustable - it has 3 different light levels .The screen is a matte anti-glare screen - I usually prefer a glossy screen (like Apple products) since the images seems clearer in a dark room, but this screen has a wide viewing angle and performs better in daylight, and brightly lit settings, like the kind you'd  find in a Starbucks. The only drawback I noticed is that the internal fan comes on at times when the laptop is under light usage, and it can take a while for it to turn off ( and it's a bit noisy ). I've read some laptop forums where people are searching for a fan control program that will work. Hopefully, Lenovo will provide one as an update. I would have given it 5 stars if it had the glossy screen and did not have that minor issue with the fan noise. But, even with that, it's a nice computer and I would definitely recommend it.

review_title: Fake pentile 4K display. Not real 4K. Do not buy and expect 4K.
review_text: As far as portable 15.6-inchers go, this one's not bad. However, you are being deceived.This laptop advertises a screen resolution of 4K UHD 3840x2160, but that isn't a complete truth. It's using what's called the RG/BW Pentile matrix, a cheap trick to achieve the ability to advertise as 3840x2160, without actually achieving the full detail of the resolution itself. You can do a web search on this type of display to learn all you'd like, but without getting too technical here, it basically means even though the screen makes your computer render this resolution, you don't get to see all that detail on your screen, because it's missing half of its pixels.Lots of reviews talk about how nice the display is. The reason for that is because many people buying new laptops today will have had old laptops with the old standard 1366x768 TN displays. This is a huge upgrade from those, but so are all the normal 1080p IPS displays you can get in other laptops half this price. Real 4K UHD 3840x2160 resolution is a huge upgrade from THIS display, and it is a disrespect to laptops that do truly achieve the resolution, that this one gets to advertise right along side them. It's not close to the tier of real-4K displays, and not even as good as the 3K 2880x1620 displays available in some laptops, such as the older ASUS UX51vz.In my opinion, you should not buy this laptop. The Dell XPS 15 and Lenovo Y700 UHD both offer the same GPU, but have a real 3840x2160 display. The ASUS may have more RAM or a bigger SSD, but those should be low priority in your decision process because they can be easily installed after-market, whereas you're pretty much stuck with this display. The Dell XPS 15 and Lenovo Y700 UHD are truly worthy choices, whereas the ASUS UX501 thrives on deception. Don't buy it.I have attached two images to this review. One is a closeup of the Dell XPS 15's display, and one is a closeup of a false-4K display such as the one in this laptop. Notice how only every other pixel can contribute to each primary color.

review_title: Good bang for the buck if price is right
review_text:
This is a good bang for the buck laptop.  The biggest plus is the inclusion of both an Intel i5 CPU and Nvidia GeForce MX150 GPU at a low price point.  The top and back are plastic but when opened, the palm rest and keyboard border have an attractive brushed metal appearance accented by a nice quality backlit keyboard.  I've seen some pretty cheesy looking backlit keyboards, so to have one that rivals the look and feel of MacBook keyboards at this price is pretty good. The laptop chassis is attractive but is a fingerprint magnet.  I attached a photo showing the smudges and fingerprints that accumulated from a brief period of light use.  My fingers were clean, neither oily nor moist.  The finish just easily attracts smudges and fingerprints.  The laptop has two USB 2 ports, one always-powered USB 3 port, one USB-C port, one HDMI port in addition to a headphone/speaker jack and surprisingly, a gigabit ethernet port.  No dongles are necessary if a hardwired connection is preferred or required for certain tasks.  Like most newer laptops, there is no optical drive.The TN panel display quality is okay but it's easily the weak link in the package.  The viewing angles are pretty bad, even directly in front.  Colors are washed out and blacks are rendered pretty poorly.  Brighter scenes aren't too bad but darker scenes can look pretty awful at times as shown in the photo I included.  Thankfully, it's only certain shaded screens that look that bad.  For the most part, the display is okay.  Obviously, there had to be a compromise somewhere to stay at this price point and I feel the display drew the short straw.  The screen is fine for gaming and desktop use but if you plan to perform photo editing, graphic design or simply want a more richly saturated crisp display, an exterior monitor is the way to go.  I have this hooked up via HDMI to a 27" ViewSonic LED monitor that's also 1080p.As far as gaming, I have no complaints so far.  This laptop easily plays Overwatch on medium settings at the native 1080p resolution at 60fps with very few drops in framerate.  It also runs reasonably well on the high setting.  I tried epic and ultra and they both run fine in training mode but aren't as stable in actual gaming.  I found that medium is the best bet to avoid any potential issues.  This will handle most games at medium or lower settings and is great for casual gamers or heavy STEAM users as long as the graphics aren't insanely demanding.Battery life is disappointing so far.  It's rated at seven hours but I get about three hours of moderate use from a full charge.  I haven't tried gaming on battery yet but I can only assume it would significantly shorten battery life even more if I'm only getting three hours from desktop use and the integrated graphics chip rather than the Nvidia GPU.  However, I'm not too worried.  I've learned that many batteries need an adjustment period.  I had a similar problem with my Note 8 phone.  In the beginning, I barely got a day's use out of the battery.  Now, I can go two to three days on a single charge.  I also did not remove all of the Acer bloatware.  I uninstalled the majority of bloatware which included an MS Office trial, a 30-day Norton Security trial and several Win 10 apps.  I left the Acer Care Center and Quick Access programs installed because they actually offer useful features such as automatically checking for manufacturer updates and quick access to many features and settings.  However, if battery life doesn't eventually improve, I may uninstall those as well to see if it helps.As usual, the Win 10 setup was annoying.  I disabled Cortana immediately, paid particular attention to the privacy questions and was greeted by a super long Windows update during setup.  The 3GB update took over two hours to complete.  Nearly all of the time was spent on the installation because the 3GB download completed quickly over a gigabit connection. At least the installation is optional during the initial setup and can be postponed.So, do I recommend this laptop?  Yes, if it's priced closer to $500 than $600.  If it's closer to $600, it might be worth dropping an extra hundred to step up to a machine like the

  
Newest Acer Nitro Flagship High Performance 15.6" FHD Gaming Laptop PC | Intel Core i5-7300HQ Quad-Core | NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 | 8GB RAM | 1TB HDD | Windows 10 | Windows Mixed Reality Ultra Ready









  
  
    
  or the

  
MSI GL62M 7RD-1407 15.6" Full HD Thin and Light Performance Gaming Laptop i5-7300HQ GTX 1050 2G 8GB 256GB SSD Win10 SteelSeries Keyboard









  
  
    
  .  Both these machines have comparable features along with the more capable GeForce GTX 1050 GPU.  The Acer even throws in a better quality IPS display.  Both sell for just under $700.  As long as this laptop is priced closer to $500, it's a decent deal.

review_title: Great mobile gaming experiance for a good price
review_text: This laptop is amazing.Pros:FAST - Able to run ME:A on max settings without stutters.Durable - The laptop is solid... even the hinges. Nothing feels cheap.Keyboard - excellent layout with great key spacing, featuring function keys that you actually use. Backlit keys.Heat management - The fan is fantastic at keeping the laptop cool, even during extended gaming sessions.Display - Matte screen (no glare).Ports galore! 4X USB, displayport, HDMI out, RJ45 and headphone jack, as well as the "new" USB type I'm not sure whats called.Price - This is about as good a deal you can expect to find for this level of performance.Battery life - will play a AAA game using max settings (no battery saver) for about 3 hours. I'm sure you could play longer if you sacrifice performance for time, which you can easily specify.Meh:Colors can be changed. Not a biggie for me, but some people enjoy it.Speakers - Typical laptop. Not good, not bad. Meh.Tackpad - its there. Meh.Bluetooth - nice to have, sometimes.ASUS gaming software - many options for enabling game port forwarding QOS stuff. I don't use it, but it will likely be attractive for enthusiasts.Cons:Display has a "green glow" around the edges during full-black sequences. From what I can tell, this is on every one and not just mine.Bloatware - the windows store automatically downloads a bunch of garbage that takes a few mins to remove.Camera - Sucks. But, you didn't buy this for the camera, right?Microphone - Even worse than the camera. Trying to use the on board mic with teamspeak was cacophonic. Most gamers will use a headset, but if not, beware the mic.CD-ROM - this was likely an error on my part, because I didn't specify to upgrade to the Blu-ray. A regular CD ROM is useless in today's digital game purchasing age. Don't be me, get the Blu-ray option.Overall, a fantastic gaming laptop for a very good price. You can tell ASUS put some work into making this a good product, which, by itself, is admirable nowadays.

It's been about two months since I've had this laptop and I feel like I've had enough time learning and reviewing it so heres my review:Pros:- i7-7700 HQ Quadcore CPU up to 3.8ghz- Nvidia 1050ti  with 4GB DDR5- Both an SSD and HDD (Although you can always add these yourselves, it was nice to have come with both)- Cooling system is one of the best Ive seen so far (Includes an Ultra-Boost button to give you extra cooling, but never needed to use it.)- Fan disperses air away from the back screen of the laptop, rather than the side of the keyboard. (I prefer this design better)- Red Backlit keyboard (Color cant be changed, but I wasnt specifically looking for a flashy laptop so this is just a plus)- Overall Matte Black texture around the laptop with pleasing MSI dragon logo on the back screen.- AntiGlare Screen- Num. Pad keyboard- Comes with 1 year manufacturer warranty(US) (You'll have to activate it online yourself.)Cons:- Although aesthetically pleasing, the Matte Black Plastic Finish is a FINGERPRINT/OIL magnet and takes more than just a dry cloth to remove- 8GB RAM (I intend to add on another 8GB stick in the nearby future)- Battery life is ridiculous when playing games- Fans are REALLY loud when playing games (Not much of a problem if you wear headphones, and is expected as it does a splendid job keeping the laptop cool)- Speakers are subpar (Again, not much of a problem if you wear headphones)Overall, I was in the market specifically for a laptop that had a good CPU/GPU, and both an SSD and HDD. I stumbled upon many competitor laptops along the same price range however, some were missing an SSD or HDD, or had the regular 1050 GPU which comes with only half (2GB) of dedicated memory of what the Ti model has (4GB). If I had purchased those laptops instead, and added on a separate SSD OR HDD, the total cost spent would be above $1000. The laptop is surprisingly light for a gaming laptop, and comes in a sleek yet aggressive theme, which wasn't what I was in the market for but is a plus to me. Most people who game on laptops would know that you get better frames while plugged in to the charger (This is due to bottlenecking of either the CPU or GPU demanding more power, yet the battery cannot provide that power alone), so the low gaming battery life is not much of a problem considering you should be plugged in to get the best performance, and the battery life outside of gaming is average (4-6 hours) depending on what work you'll be doing. Ultimately, the laptop met more than my needs and was in my price range ($899, $960~ after taxes), and I expect to be using it throughout and well after the years of college.

Update February 12, 2020: This is the worst laptop I have ever owned, and I have had a couple really crappy ones. Pretty sure that this laptop is officially dead, no warning other than one blue screen a day or so ago. Was turned away from it, with it plugged in and charging while I played a game on my xbox, turn back to check my cell phone and not a single light was on. Assumed maybe it came unplugged, maybe plug wasnt working, maybe its the cord.. long story short its none of those things its definitely the laptop. Never will I buy a MSI computer ever again. Not even sure I will ever touch the parts again. Not planning to contact the company because their customer service has been rude and unhelpful every time I have spoken to them about any of their products/services. I saw an affordable laptop, with decent specs from a name that seemed trusted in the tech community, and I went for it. Don't waste your money on their products. Please, maybe spend a little more on something from a brand with less issues. If this is how they handled this laptop with its issues when it was fresh to market, I can't imagine they behave any better about their newer models.I have really mixed feelings about this laptop. I like the design, and theoretically the stats are pretty good. In use, it doesn't work out quite so well. I knew I would need to upgrade the ram, but out of the box this computer has always been on the slower side. It can play some games fine but struggles with several. For example, multiplayer games like Terraria to games like Black Desert Online seem to make this laptop struggle to keep up. And no, its not my internet connection. My internet can handle 3 people streaming and two people playing mmo's without really breaking a sweat. On the laptop I lose frames, it freezes up now and then, crashes the games, and the fans kick on their high setting at a moments notice. Which are very very loud by the way. On the plus side, the laptop doesn't overheat much.The display is really poor quality. Trying to watch or play anything where the movie or game intends it to be dim or look like night time is pretty bad because it all starts to look the same. I have tried to adjust these settings with the programs provided but it seems to not make much of a difference.The battery life on this is awful, but I knew that when I bought it. It doesn't take a year to charge up, so I don't gripe much on it. However, the location and charger style is incredibly inconvenient. A laptop meant for gamers, in a world where the majority is right handed, puts one usb slot on the right side not far from the charge port, where the cord design lines up the charger cord to run along the side of the laptop. Plug-in mouse setup can be annoying because I either have to fix the charger to point out the back (which would be fine if it weren't for the point of laptops to be travel) or it overlaps my mouse usb and the charge cord aomwtimes will get in the way. Its a minor design annoyance, but I felt was worth mentioning.Last but not least, the built in camera is useless. First, it tries to make you pay for the ability to use the camera because it doesnxt come already registered or with a code for the software that makes the camera operable. I sought assistance on the MSI site and felt treated a little rudely when offered a solution. The solution was a little convoluted but worked, where I also felt like I had been thrown back in time to my old baseball sized logitech webcam from when I was a kid. I live decently far from family so skype calls are important to me so I can catch up with them and see how they are. The camera quality is rough. And then, amusingly enough, the camera stopped working again entirely. It doesn't detect that I have one, regardless of installing or uninstalling drivers or anything else. The whole camera saga really irritated me. It decided not to exist right before a discord D&D session. Embarassing and frustrating to go through all the crap to make the camera work (This is how it is shipped by the way, not an accident in set up or anything! They literally put webcam hardware in the laptop that they don't bother having registered the software. I've never experieced this in my life, so it boggles my mind that this is standard for this laptop) only to have it become useless again. So if cameras aren't that important, I suppose don't worry about it. Or if they are and you have your heart set on this laptop, just save yourself the frustration and buy a camera to plug in.On the plus side, I enjoy the size, shape, weight, and design of the laptop. I appreciate the cooling abilities. MSI is a company I generally like a lot, and I don't feel like this laptop represents the quality of their company as a whole. With a little love, patience, and a chunk of money I can fix most of the issues I have with this computer. My bone to pick is that when you buy a laptop like this, you shouldn't have to go through all this when most other laptops (Especially with this pricetag) work as intended right out of the box. I've owned and worked with laptops ranging from crappy tiny netbooks to macbook pros. These are problems I only ever encountered on low end computers, except the camera. That was a doozy, and a new one for me.Oh! Advice in regards to the harddrivev before you set anything else up after you get it up and running, change the drive locations of your folders like Documents, Downloads, Pictures, etc. Use the main hard drive mostly for the operating system (sincr its small) and put everything else on the secondary drive. That is how it is intended and will save you drom MSI alerts constantly telling you your HD is full. I forgot a couple times and installed things on the main HD instead and the pop ups were a mild nuisance.If i find better solutions for some of these problems, I will update my review with how I got it fixed. I bought this laptop in February 2018, Reviewing it November 2018.

review_title: Great specs, decent battery life, good price
review_text: I was undecided between 4 or 5 stars, but I decided to go for 5. Here is why.My initial idea was to buy the new MacBook Pro. Given the price and the specs, I decided to do some research and look for some valid alternatives. Then I came across this model of the ASUS ZenBook.The price is definitely good considering the specs: core i7 2.7GHz, 16GB RAM 2133MHz,  512GB SSD hard drive, very nice screen and interesting quad-speaker audio configuration. For comparison, note that the MacBook Pro 13'' comes with a slower processor (without boosting given the absence of fan), slower RAM (i.e., 1600MHz), and if you want the same SSD capacity you'll need over $1000 more.The ZenBook fan almost never starts (unless heavy computation is performed), and personally I consider it very quiet. Good quality of manufacturing and materials, with a very nice design. The only potential issue with the laptop could be due to the single USB-C port, but the laptop comes with a nice hub that is more than enough for my needs. Plus a very nice leather-like case, that is also a plus.The battery honestly lasts from 5 to 6 hours, depending on the usage. This is the only point that you could not be 100% satisfied about. But given the form-factor and the power of this machine, really thinking about it I'm amazed on how they even reached that battery life. Disappointing integrated webcam, but I really do not care about it. If you care about it, that's gonna be a no-no.Points to remember: it is a 12.5-inches, so the screen is small (very nice and bright, but small), the actual battery life is ~5-6h, the webcam is disappointing. If you are ok with that, you'll be super-satisfied by this machine because of the amazing performances and very nice and clean design.Personal advice: install Linux, it works like a charm :)

review_title: Good Second Machine If You Can Get it On Sale
review_text: I've had this for about a week. First, the good: low price, portable, surprisingly solid construction for a cheap laptop, flash storage makes it faster than a spinning hard drive. Keyboard feels *alright*. 64GB model has enough space for a few important programs, unlike the 32GB. Screen is also decent for this price range, and is a good bit larger than the 11". Also, the screen flexes all the way down which is cool if not super useful. I do some basic work in MS Office and it has been fine with that.Now, the bad: trackpad is horrible. Although mine does have 2-finger scroll (it was very inconsistent when first setting it up), the overall trackpad is terrible. In Word, it zooms on its own, opens Cortana unprompted, etc.Speakers and mic are low quality, hard to hear Skype convos. This can be avoided with a $5 two way earbud. The web browsing experience can slow down on pages with lots of script (CNN, etc..). 2GB RAM ought to be enough to handle basic browsing, and you can load the page, but it is not especially crisp and fluid. It does get the job done though.Bottom line: this computer needs about $15 in accessories (wireless mouse, earbuds with a mic) to be a decent little PC for Word, web browsing, Skype, and email. If you can get it for a discount it is a good buy.

I will likely post a more comprehensive review after a few weeks. I just received this laptop today.My background. I am a PC enthusiast and have been for about 23 years. I build my own desktop PCs and I am into some gaming, cad work, business applications, general web browsing.Initial impressions: this laptop is on the larger side for a 15.6".. a little on the heavy side. I had some issues with the screen going black during setup, as if it were going into sleep mode and sometimes while I was typing. I thought there might be a hardware problem at first. Finally up and running.Once I had it all set up and running... this thing runs GREAT. For general use, I would say almost on par with my new i7-7700K rig that I built a few months ago.When opening apps and web browsing, it is very fast and there is no lag with this hardware (I will never own another PC without a SSD for the OS). It is very snappy and I am very happy with the performance. I have not tried any games yet. Will do so soon. The display is very nice; colors look great, and it has a wide viewing angle. There is a bit of light bleed during dark times (such as boot up).. not a huge deal at this point. The keyboard... at first I notice it flexing a bit. However, after typing on it for a bit, it feels very sturdy and the keys solid and have a great feel overall. I wouldn't say it's as good as a mechanical keyboard but you aren't going to get any better on a laptop. It's good. I usually struggle a bit when typing on a flat keyboard but seem to be adapting to this one much easier than usual. Probably due to the long travel of the keys. I'm pretty impressed with it. Also the keyboard back lighting is very nice and easily adjustable with the Asus software. Nice touch.Cons: none yet, stay tuned.Edit: after 24 hours, I had a persistent problem with this laptop entering sleep mode while typing on the keyboard. PROPS to AMAZON for an easy return and speedy replacement. No issues with replacement and this laptop is a good buy. Runs great, would buy again without hesitation.

review_title: Just like the other review stated
review_text: I'm writing this review as I use the laptop. Just like the other review stated, this thing is as close as you can get to a macbook. This Acer does not make a single noise. I put my ear up to it attempting to hear the smallest of movements but I just heard silence. As I'm writing this review, the bottom of the laptop is not even warm. It's almost cold to the touch. After setting it up, removing a bunch of bloatware, disabling a bunch of unnecessary startup programs, this thing starts up lightning fast. I'm talking 5-10 seconds max (from pressing the power button to the computer being unlocked). From a sleeping point maybe 2-3 seconds from pressing the button to unlocking it. The design is awesome, the keyboard is great for typing, and the back-lit keyboard is useful. So far I've been using this laptop just for using small applications and web browsing (I've been using it for 3 hours now with normal brightness) and the remaining estimated battery life is 4 hours and 33 minutes as I type (68% remaining). The metal it's made out of feels nice. The laptop is only about 3.3lbs so it's definitely portable. Everything runs super smoothly on this laptop since it has the latest gen i5-7200u processor (great processor btw) 8gb of memory and a 256gb SSD.The only thing I would complain about this laptop is the brightness might not be suitable for everyone. For me - a usually indoor laptop user - the brightness is perfect. But I can see how a some people might want a brighter screen.Overall, I doubt there's a better laptop than this for $600.

review_title: Good laptop, I should have bought the 14"
review_text: So far so good, just a bit bigger in size than I expected.  I have an Acer Chromebook similarly clad in aluminum, only it has an aluminum bottom which stays cool on my legs.  This laptop has a plastic bottom that seems to acclimate to my body temperature making it more comfortable.  I can't see where the plastic bottom would be a negative feature.  The keyboard is comfortable enough for a laptop, and for the most part the key layout is okay.  Startup time is fast and the finger print reader if fairly accurate unlocking the screen.  From sleep mode, when the lid is closed, to startup is really fast, nearly instant.  WiFi connection on my home network is solid, Bluetooth has good range and easily paired to my wireless mouse and Bluetooth headphone, battery life seems excellent getting a whole day off the charger. The screen is clean and bright with good view angles.  Just not sure if I like the glossy screen. as it's a bit reflective.

review_title: Really impressed with the attention to detail
review_text: So far I absolutely love this laptop!  It's lightning fast thanks to the SSD and latest-gen i5, and the 8GB of RAM allow it to handle multitasking really well.  It also boots and hibernates super quickly.  All of that becoming more standard these days, but what really makes this laptop stand out is the quality and attention to detail that go beyond the specs.  The keyboard is almost certainly the best laptop keyboard I have ever owned, the keys feel so solid, responsive, and wonderfully contoured and positioned that it's just a joy to type on. The trackpad is very nice as well. Another highlight is the high-quality Wifi card: My apartment has very weak signal so I was amazed when I turned this on and it effortlessly streamed HD video. During normal operation this laptop is totally silent, and even in the very rare cases where the fan spins up to full speed it is still really quiet.  The display is beautiful, I'm used to laptops with TN screens so I was blown away by this amazing IPS display.  The fact that it's full HD means you probably need to use at least 125% Windows display scaling, but that's not a big deal and a good tradeoff for being able to play FHD video etc. (Hint: I have discovered Firefox is much better than Chrome at interacting properly with display scaling.)  I've also found that if you want a reasonably long battery life you'll need to lower the resolution, but that's not a big deal to me. The screen also has a wide variety of brightness settings which I appreciate.Perhaps most important is the build quality and durability.  This is hard to judge after only a week or so of use, but it feels much more solid and well-made than any of my previous laptops.  There's none of the squeaking, bending, and flexing that have plagued other models.  Everything just feels rock solid and built to last.  There were a couple of touches that really impressed me here: the hinge (a major weak point on most laptops) is made entirely of metal, and the laptop features a drainage system to provide resistance to liquid spills.  I'll update my review if anything breaks down but right now I'm very optimistic. And the great thing is despite being so solid it's relatively light weight and slim.I only have a few small quibbles. The headphone jack is placed very awkwardly, as it's exactly where most right-handed people would use an external mouse. Also, the function key is in the lower left corner, with the ctrl key to the right of it. This definitely takes some getting used to, as normally ctrl is in the corner. Given how frequently ctrl is used in business applications, one would have thought Lenovo would have swapped these keys, but no such luck.  And while I love Windows 10 Pro, the process of upgrading to it (for free) through Lenovo recovery is far from easy, intuitive, or convenient. I really wish it just came preloaded. And as expected the integrated graphics card won't really cut it for graphically intensive work or games.But all in all, this is an excellent machine, and a great value at the $900 price Amazon is currently selling it for. If, like me, you're fed up with machines that offer great specs at a great price but cut corners on the details, I think you'll love the T460.

Solid build quality.  I really like the keyboard - it feels high quality and has very good travel distance for a slim laptop.  This machine has good performance and sufficient battery life if you're using it for basic office type computing and browsing.As for Cons:  Ranked in order of importance to me, here are the things that bring take it down to four stars: - Trackpad - laggy and annoying. review_title: What an amazing laptop. Buy this over the Dell XPS 13 and LG Gram, it's better and it'll still be cheaper.
review_text: I am an engineering college student who is super picky about their computer specs and hardware. I was also on a tight budget and in need of solid value laptop that would last me for the next few years. I've been looking for several months and trying to pick the best laptop for under $1000. I was torn between this laptop, the LG Gram, and the Dell XPS 13. Now that I've owned this laptop for a few months, I am so glad I didn't buy the others.I use this laptop for Microsoft Office, online homework, and for keeping all of my college homework files with me and accessible on the fly. This laptop has changed the whole college game for me. Not only is it so light and portable, but it is such a pleasure to use that I find myself actually looking forward to homework just so I can pull it out and use it.Pros:1) Fingerprint reader: what an awesome little part. Logging in is reliable and super quick with the reader. It also looks really cool on the laptop, and doesn't retract from the touchpad at all.2) 256 M.2 SSD: This is a must have. This laptop shuts down and boots over twice as fast as my iPhone 7. I couldn't ask for more.3) 3200x1800 resolution screen: This resolution packed into a 13.3 inch IPS display is such eye candy that I can't imagine having even a 1080p screen. The IPS looks very nice as well, with solid color reproduction.4) Precision Touchpad: The touchpad has a perfect blend of grip and slickness, and it's always reliable. It feels much like a Macbook Air touchpad.5) Keyboard: The keyboard keys and travel feel much like a Macbook Air as well, very comfortable to type on. The keys are right where your fingers expect them, and you will be at home on this keyboard in just the first time using.6) Battery life: the battery is seriously impressive for the resolution of the screen and the brightness it can reach. I take my laptop with me all day to college without a charger, and I'll come home with at least 60% left with around 50% brightness all day.7) Noise: I undervolted the CPU and GPU using Intel XTU, and now the cooler fan never comes on. The laptop stays cold, quiet, and efficient. Even when the fan does come on, it's at the lowest speed and not on for long.8) The i5-7200U is overkill for everyday college tasks on this computer, but it's still very nice to have because the laptop is doesn't stutter even for a second with anything. After undervolting, my CPU doesn't thermal throttle at all either.9) Portability: This laptop weighs 2.4 lbs, and is so sleek that it fits in any size backpack. Looks very nice as well, very similar to a Macbook Air. People compliment the circular lid etching on this laptop all the time.10) Ports: It has all the necessary ports: USB-C, USB 3.1, USB 2, headphone jack, memory card reader, and mini HDMI. All while having the thin form factor11) Sound: This laptop has speakers that are about as good as they get on these thin ultrabook laptops. Only the Macbook Pro sounds better, but that is in a whole other price range.12) Keyboard Backlight: Not all laptops of this thin form factor have backlit keyboards. This one has 3 brightness levels, which is hugely appreciated.Cons:1) The anti-glare coating on the screen does work well, and does reduce lots of glare. However, the display would be much crisper with the UHD if it was glossy. This would increase glare though, but this is my personal preference.2) Screen size: 13.3 inches is nice for a compact laptop, but it would definitely be nice to have something like 15 inches. The price difference is pretty hefty to upgrade to the bigger size, but I figured I'd mention this anyway.3) The VGA camera is very basic and unappealing. This was obviously a compromise to cut costs, but it's okay because it works fine. It isn't high res or high fps, but it can get the job done.Don't hesitate to buy this laptop, just make sure to buy the 3200x1800 display with the fingerprint reader if you do!

review_title: So far so good. Nice computer
review_text: So far so good. Nice computer. Love the picture quality, and plenty fast from what I've seen so far. Like a lot of the others, I also added the extra stick of ram and SSD. They really did make it easy to add the extra hardware. The Samsung migration software was also pretty quick and smooth, save for a couple minor issues. Some of the articles I read did not mention disconnecting the original drive after moving over the OS, and before booting from the new SSD. I read this was the cause of some errors. I also read that a fresh install of the OS was a better idea than to clone. In the end, I decided to try the migration software, and clone the main drive. Figured if I ran into issues, I would then reformat and do a fresh install. Here's what I did. First thing was to run all windows updates. I then created a bootable USB drive in case I needed to start fresh. After installing the SSD, install the samsung data migration software, run the program to copy the OS from the HDD to the SSD. Once it copies over, shut down the computer. Disconnect the HDD, start it up, and it should now boot from the SSD. Confirm everything works, shut it down again, reconnect the original drive, and start it again. I should note. When I did this, I noticed the original drive wasn't automatically showing up. After checking, I noticed it was due to an error/conflict with the disk volume serial number, because of this, the drive was offline. I just went to disk management, selected the drive to go online. The error then seemed to go away and I was able to read and reformat the drive. After doing this, everything seemed normal until I tried using the windows search (taskbar) function. In some instances, it would show up, but the actual function would not work. I.e. windows update wouldn't work. Tried multiple "fixes" including the command prompt SFC repair tool ( sfc / scannow ), but none seemed to work. The one fix that finally worked was to create a new ADMIN user. Once I logged in under the new user, everything seemed to work fine. I then deleted the other user account, and now everything appears to be in order. The one thing that needs improvement is the sound. There's distortion at about 90%, and it's not even close to being "loud".

While the internal functioning of this laptop is reasonable (aside form running windows 10 which I just don't like), the external features leave much to be desired.The MOST annoying feature of this laptop is the power button.  It is located along the right edge (facing outward, like on a phone or tablet) and is in the exact place where most people position their hands to carry it from one place to another.  This means that I (and every other user of this laptop I know) am constantly accidentally turning it off when I merely meant to move it from one place to another.  Whether picking it up or merely pushing it to the left, this is a problem.  Then, if that wasn't trouble enough, when I push the power button to turn it back on, nothing happens.  Nothing.  It's like there is a timer or something that makes the power button not work until enough time has passed.  In addition, sometimes the button shuts the laptop completely off and sometimes it puts it to sleep.  As far as I can tell, there is no way to know which it will do.  (There is a setting that allows you to disable this button, but I'm not sure you'd want to do that (will it come back on if you shut down from the menu??) and my place of business has disabled that feature for me anyway)  Next, I have no idea what button or action actually wakes it back up after it falls asleep on its own.  Sometimes its the power button, sometimes the space bar, sometimes the touch pad.  Sometimes I have to shut it and wait that undetermined amount of time before the power button works again.  Lastly, while one would expect that closing the laptop would put it to sleep and opening it would wake it up, this doesn't seem to always be the case either.  Sometimes it stays on and gets really warm after I close it.  Sometimes nothing seems to wake it up (and I know what you thinking - yes it was fully charged).The other feature that I find annoying is the keyboard.  It has mostly reasonably sized keys and is easy to use (I remember reading or being told that it has some lining underneath to prevent liquids from damaging the inner workings, which is great!  I can't tell you how many times I've dripped or spilled or sneezed on my laptop and it keeps going).  Except for the arrows and page-up/page-down buttons.  They are half the size of everything else. I accidentally hit the wrong one on a daily basis.Just to be clear, my place of business chose this machine for me and everyone else to use.  They are very durable (I've dropped it, knocked it into things, slammed it closed, spilled things, closed a pencil in it, etc, and it keeps on going).  Unfortunately, my place of business has disabled lots of settings this year (after a few people made a grave mistake...).  Last year we had more control, but the issues I speak of have been present from day one (two years ago) and everyone has them.I will say though, I LOVE the touch screen.  It is a very useful feature I didn't think I'd like this much.  Tablet mode - meh (but I think that's a windows 10 issue anyway).  Worst thing about tablet mode is the location of that stupid power button...

Doing well so far. I do not see any screen bleeding. Tried getting Windows/BIOS/Nvidia drivers updated at work. Let me say that you will want to immediately remove the startup sound set in the BIOS... super annoying. I will report back on specs and performance.UPDATE:Still need to look into the BIOS issues (VT-x or RAID settings or overclocking manually), but the monitor is NOT 60hz, it is 75hz (which was awesome to find out, since ACER and everyone else keeps saying it is 60hz). Gsync does work with the monitor (once you update the BIOS). No screen bleeding or stuttering. No heat issues. No issues with Windows, except ones that Windows caused themselves. I have been playing Conan with ultimate settings and have not went over 60C. Hard drives a bit slow, but not a big issue. Only wish they were not RAID 0, especially since I have spent hours downloading updates for games via Steam. Thought I'd want the DVD drive, but now all games require online activation and updating day 1, so it doesn't really need this. Hardly any bloatware (office 365 trial and maybe 2 others). Software from ACER is great, especially Predatorsense, which allows overclocking, but the optimization software could be a bit better like AVG:PC Tuneup. I will try to keep updating this. Great buy so far! Only complaint is the locked BIOS and RAID setup at the moment. Build is solid. Keyboard is amazing, but could be recessed a bit more for comfort. Trackpad is great, but a bit sticky, as there is a bit of friction with the material they chose, which may go away after use anyway. Keyboard is zoned backlighting but looks great. Fans are quiet. I don't see what everyone was talking about when it came to the fans being noisey. WIFI is super fast. I think I may have covered all the issues I have seen reported... I think they were just one-offs. Colors display great on monitor with a good refresh rate. Power cord is shaped a bit strange, as it lies across the cd drive, due to a 90 degree turn in the cord at the computer-side plug. Sound is good enough. Oh, the symbol on the back DOES light up, along with the running stripes on the back. I dislike that my window key is disabled when the trackpad is turned off, but I understand why they did this. Just wish I had a way to turn off the backlighting at the push of a button, but there may be a way to do this that I haven't found yet(except for running off of battery). I got some Kryonaut paste (the best for novices), but I don't think I will ever need it, even with overclocking in Turbo mode. You get a little over 2-hr of web time on battery and probably more if you adjust powersaving options. KillerEthernet program is great for blocking programs from using your bandwidth. I will hopefully be able to try to break RAID, as advised per the ACER boards, and get an NVMe SSD. I guess most of the BIOS settings people are concerned about can be adjusted from Windows or software, just like this RAID setting (and overclocking and G-sync, which also required the BIOS update and VT-x, which I am told is already enabled by default) I will try to update with info about this and if it does truly allow VT-x for Virtual Machines and if I ever move away from the RAID setup.  I am rambling. I would say to go ahead and buy this one! Feel free to leave questions... I will try to check back.

The trackpad is decently sized and works fine; although it is not super precise, but I use the laptop mostly as desktop replacement, connected to wireless mouse and keyboard.The LCD screen is pretty nice and bright; refresh rate is great; and works fine for most of the activities; but I have the laptop connected to a bigger monitor on my desk, so I don't use it all the time. Colors are pretty bright and vivid; took a bit to calibrate it but then you can let it be and enjoy it.The keyboard is awesome; I feel very comfortable typing on it; and the resistance and spacing of the keys is perfect for me (I have big hands); I still make mistakes because the layout of the keyboard on the right side is not the same as a standard PC keyboard; but once you remember that the delete key is right on top of the backspace, and that the enter key is not as big as it was, then it is a breeze. Plus it has a ton of light settings; not a fan of flashy ones, but the red hue is quite nice.CPU and GPU works great; got some awesome results from 3dsmax, Visual Studio and other Adobe apps like Photoshop and Dimension; which made me very happy, since the main usage of this computer is portable graphic workstation. Unity works great too, and with 16 GB of RAM, you have plenty to run concurrent and memory-intensive apps.SSD is small; and it is weird since it is a raid made of 2x128 GB M2 drive; but it works fast and it is fine for me. The computer has a 1 TB mechanical drive, which won't win any contest for speed, but it is reliable and awesome to have inside the computer, to store large amount of data.The computer comes with a DVD combo drive, which can be swapped for an extra fan; I did ditch both and got an extra caddy to put an extra SATA SSD drive; and the process was painless. Now I have 2 TB of storage plus the 256 GB of system drive, and all without opening the laptop or buy external enclosures.Sound is OK; I didn't buy it for that, the internal audio card works as expected with headphones; and the internal speakers are quite loud and nice to listen to; but for movie watching, use your headphones.The fan is not that loud; not sure where you live, but in my office room, with everything else going on, I can't hear it at all, even when it is full throttle. I never got the laptop very hot, neither when playing games nor rendering in 3dsmax or working in Unity; so I guess I was lucky with the thermal compound job they did at the factory.Games run fast here; got Witcher 3 at max details and it runs smooth as silk; same for other games that are very demanding, like Tomb Raider. The scores for 3dmark are a bit lower than a desktop overclocked 1070 with an i7 8th gen; due to the fact that the laptop versions are usually clocked lower for power and heat management issues, but I won't loose my sleep for few frames lost. If you are a purist, get a desktop computer.Battery life is a joke, but this is a desktop replacement. The main issue is the lack of energy saving process, which would switch to the Intel onboard GPU, but this does not happen; the 1070 is always on and this means that the battery goes down fast (about 2.5 hours of usage, 50m if rendering). Plugged in, no problem, but if you plan to move around with this beast in tow; keep in mind that you need to be close to a plug most of the time (although in this case, you would get an ultra light model).Software onboard was not super intrusive; I did remove the extras I do not need; and left the Acer app, that is great for backup, restore and overall managing the computer drivers and get the info like serial number and such. W10 works just fine.It has 4 USB3 ports on the sides, and 1 USB-C Thunderbolt; so if you plan to use an external GPU one day, you can do so. Future proof is great.The other ports are the power connector; a SD card reader (always welcome to avoid to use a dongle), and a display port (full port, thank God) and a HDMI port, with the LAN port to guarantee connectivity at top speed. It has also a mic and headphone jack, which are also great.VR works great on this computer; the Rift runs smooth and nicely; setup was easy and also using external monitors works great (got an ultra-wide screen connected to it).In conclusion; great specs, decent price for what you get, and VR ready; perfect as game machine and as workstation; can't really complain much about anything.
