review_title: A Great Gaming Laptop for Under $1200
review_text: TL;DR - This laptop is great for its price, and you aren't gonna find much better. The screen is OK, the battery life is OK, and the thermals/fan noise is OK, however everything else is very solid and the i7-7700hq and 1060 (Even though it has 3gb of vram) are more than enough for running games at 1080p 60fps and should still be able to hold out for 3-4 years. I definitely recommend it.The Asus FX502VM-AS73 (wow thats a mouthful) was, when i first looked at it, a great deal for some great hardware. Thankfully, I just recieved mine yesterday and everything was in a good working condition and there was no damage to the packaging or the laptop itself. I did buy from amazon warehouse, but it was listed as Used-Like New and in its original, pristine packaging. Luckily that was true, and I found no dead pixels on the screen, no mousepad issues, or any other problems. It's as if it just came off the shelf and they accidentally opened it or something. However, not everything is perfect with this laptop, so i'll start with the negatives first and work my way to the positivesCONS: - The screen is OK. I read a lot of reviews on amazon and saw that people said  the screen was horrible, that it had horrible viewing angles and colors, and was very laggy in general. However, I find none of these claims to really be 100% true. Yes, the screen is not the highest of quality, and is nothing like their GL502VM laptop, but it definitely is still good. The contrast ratio is not that great at 300:1, and I would have been willing to pay a little more to get something better, but they needed to cut some corners, and im glad that they did with the screen, instead of downgrading to weaker hardware. The 1080p is great though, and I still had a moment of awe when I was playing GTA V, and was chilling on my yacht looking at the sunset (I was bored, ok). It didn't look low quality at all, and for a moment i thought I was playing on a much better screen, so the screen is definitely lacking, but it's nothing to be worried about; you'll still have a great experience.- The mousepad sucks. It's very difficult to press both buttons at the same time (almost impossible) and it is way too sensitive right out of the box. However, I use a mouse way more than i do with the mousepad, and only really use it when im out and about. So im not too concerned with it-The webcam sucks. Looks like its 480p. I wouldnt use it for anything other than a skype call with a best friend who doesn't really care about the crappy quality of your camera. Dont use it, please.-The arrow keys on the keyboard are way too thin in my opinion. Plus they aren't really separated from the rest of the keyboard, so it's really easy to be hitting the numpad or special keys instead of the actual arrow keys. There seems to be some space on the chassis for a little bit wider keys, or some separation, so im not so sure as to why they chose to do what they did.-The speakers aren't that great. They are good for casual things. Gaming is fine with them. I did actually like the stereo positioning of them much more than my old MSI laptop. It felt way more immersive, but there is practically no bass, so explosions and such were kind of lacking in "boom". I was listening to music and watching some videos and I wasn't appalled by the quality, so they will surely suffice for those kinds of things. However, If you are doing some kind of content creation, whether it be with music or videos, I would obviously ditch the laptop speakers and get some real speakers.NEUTRAL:-The battery life is what you'd expect for a gaming laptop. I was getting about 3 hours on casual internet surfing, and an hour while playing GTA V. I'm not sure why some people dont understand that gaming laptops do require way more wattage than a macbook or ultrabook, and fault gaming laptops for having weak batteries. Its a fact of life right now, and it'll probably be years before we start seeing gaming laptops that can run for more than 10 hours on battery life. I usually don't game when i'm not at home, and i leave it plugged in when i am home, so this really isnt much of a problem for me.-Temperatures are OK. I would say im a little surprised by the average temps with this machine, in such a small chassis. The old laptop i had was a MSI gp60-1053 leopard pro, and my god that thing was a hulk. Keep in mind that laptop had a 950m and a dual core i5-4210h. With such low specs you would have thought it could be in a slim design and stay cool, but no, oh my god that thing got hot. Usually cpu temps were in the 90's and GPU temps in the mid 80's. However, this thing, which probably has like a 500% performance increase (I haven't actually compared the two yet so obviously that's made up) has decent temps while averaging mid 80's on the CPU and mid 70's on the GPU when i was playing GTA V for 2 hours with no thermal throttling when looking at MSI afterburner. However, it still does get hot. I dont really play any games in my lap, because I just find it uncomfortable to be using a mouse on a couch or my bed, so usually the laptop will always be on my desk when i game. However, when i am moving around, it really doesnt get annoyingly hot like some people have stated in their reviews. It gets warm, but not too warm, and unless you are wearing some heavy clothing, you shouldn't really notice it if you are watching some videos or surfing the web. (BE WARNED, IF YOU USE MSI AFTERBURNER, DONT TRY TO OVERCLOCK. 99% OF LAPTOPS AREN'T MADE TO OVERCLOCK. DO1N'T GET COCKY)-Connectivity is good. 3 usb 3.1, 1 mini display port, 1 hdmi port, 1 SD card reader (which has average speeds in 80mb/s) ethernet port (Which has a interesting design where there is a flap you have to push down in order to fit the cable in, which is a big hassle and takes longer than it should) a kensington lock, and finally only one audio/microphone in jack, which could be a problem to those who have two separate for their headphones and micCONS:- The size is great. At .9 inches and 4.9lbs, this thing is a beast for it's size. It's amazing that they are able to fit such powerful hardware into a chassis this small. Im not really sure how the Max-q 1060 laptops are going to play out though, especially when it comes to laptops like these. I feel the 20% decrease in performance to achieve low thermals a small design in the max-q laptops is not really worth it. When you consider shortening it to like .7 inches, and dropping the weight to around 3 or 4 lbs, I dont find the compromise in performance to be a good trade off. I would much rather carry around 1 or 2 more lbs, just to get my moneys worth and have a fully functional laptop 1060.- On the topic of the 1060, this card is amazing. I do have a desktop with 2 970's in SLI, and while it is nowhere near as powerful as my desktop, it still blows everything out of the water. The main reason why i got this laptop was because I wanted something mobile i could take to college, so I could game on it when im not too busy with college work, but also use it in the classroom, but not have to lug around an 8 lb msi Apache laptop. The only game that I have completely tested is GTA V, but I have every setting on very high with msaa 2x on, and im getting around 50-60fps. I decided to turn down reflection quality, grass quality, and particles quality to high, and I got a jump to a solid 60fps consistently, without it looking not as good as the very high preset. I also tested unigine valley, and got 62.7FPS on the extreme HD preset, which is pretty good in my opinion, when you think about the hardware required to get a solid framerate on those benchmarks. Also, the GL502vm is basically the exact same as the fx502vm-as73, with the exception of a 1060 6GB, and a 120hz g-sync panel. First off, a 1060 will rarely use all 6gb, because it simply isnt powerful enough to, and also, 1080p gaming rarely goes above 3gb's. Unless you plan on hooking this laptop up to a 1440p monitor, the 3gb version is the way to go, and will save you $300 if you are on a budget. (It got 11721 on 3Dmark firestrike).-The intel i7-7700hq is a monster. While it only has a 8-10% increase over the 6700hq, It still is an increase, and the price jump from a 6th gen i7 to a 7th gen i7 is really not that much, maybe $20 to $30 when i look at some of the models. The 4 cores and 8 threads have killed everything i've thrown at it, and is soooo much faster than my old 2 core 4 thread i5 on my previous laptop. It scored 750cb in cinebench r15 on the multithreaded workload, and a 140cb on the single threaded workload.- The keyboard is also very nice. It has a nice, tactile feel and nothing (besides the arrow keys) is too squished to be really annoying. The red backlight keys is a nice touch, but i would have liked to seen some aspect of RGB in this day and age of RGB everything, especially when we are already playing a $1100 premium. The keyboard does get warm, but only in the middle. The WASD key and arrow keys stay cool, even while in an intense load. However, typing something while just coming off of playing an intense game, or running countless benchmarks in the background for some reason, typing becomes a little uncomfortable with the hotter keys in the middle- The storage is good. a 128gb ssd is snappy and responsive. Boots in an average of 4 seconds. You can also upgrade it with another m.2 ssd to increase storage, or get a faster samsung m.2. The 1tb sshd is also good for your steam library and general workload. Nothing much to say about it really.In general, I think that pretty much covers everything. There were some corners cut to keep this thing under $1200, but im glad they didnt sacrifice the hardware, which really makes this laptop so compelling. If you are like me, and dont feel like spending $1500+ on a laptop, especially when you dropped $2000 on a desktop, this is a great option to save some money.

Sorry I'm being so picky about the screen but it was meant to be a gaming laptop so yeah...

review_title: Dead half way through initial install, Fixed now though.
review_text: I received it Thursday. Following the instructions, I plugged it in and left it alone to charge. I came home from work Friday so excited to get on my new laptop. I turned it on, it uploaded updates, told it I preferred English and selected Express Config instead of Custom. It didn't take long. Quickly it asked me to log into Microsoft or set up an account. I got half of my email address enter and the screen went black. I can see the mouse, that's it. Left it alone, nothing. Rebooted, nothing. I open the warranty booklet and it says to go to their website for customer support info. Seriously. What if this was my only computer? Luckily, I have a phone I can look it up, but my mother doesn't. What would she do. So I look it up, hoping its an easy fix. One quick phone call and I'm ready to go for the weekend. Woot. But I won't know until next week because their support desk is only open Mon-Fri. Seriously. There is an email address and I can leave a message, which is nice. But how freaking frustrating. If/when I get the computer to function I will update this to a review of the actual product. But since I can't use it, all I can review is a complete lack to contact anyone today about the computer that didn't work basically out of the box.UPDATE: Several hours later it occurred to me to go to their website. Not the one they put in the warranty book, their normal site. I found a live chat there. It took over an hour to get someone, but then it was in fact the simple fix I hoped for. Hard reboot while holding F2. Yay. So, I'm still mildly annoyed by the whole process, but I have a laptop now. For now, I'm sticking with 3 stars because the material they provide in the box for what to do with a problem is WRONG. Don't go to the commercial Asus site. Just go to Asus.com.

review_title: Fantastic business computer with one flaw.
review_text: I have been using this computer for 7 months and so far I am beyond pleased with it. The fingerprint scanner has been working flawlessly and is a great alternative to manually entering a password every time. Speed of the computer is very impressive, it is quick and responsive since there is no bloatware loaded. After several months I upgraded the hard drive to a Samsung 500GB SSD. With that upgrade this laptop boots up and loads lightning fast. I have not upgraded the 8gb of memory as of yet but that is forthcoming as I have a tenancy to leave browser windows open in Chrome and that habit utilizes a good amount of memory. I do a light amount of HD video and photo editing and so far the processor and memory has performed well with those task. When utilized on my desk the HDMI is utilized for an external wide screen monitor, so running two screens is not an issue with the graphics card. The 27in monitor I have attached is crisp, clear and responsive.The one flaw that I have with the computer is that with the construction near the memory. When grabbed from the front corner on the left front corner I have had the computer freeze/lock up. The only fix is to force a shutdown when that happens. I have determined that plastic bottom panel covering the memory is pressing into the memory stick which is under the mouse pad and causing it to compress which causes the PC to freeze. I have 4 other ASUS computers (different models) that I use for my business and this is the only one that does this. I just have to be careful when picking it up in the field.Overall a great value and despite its one flaw it is a solid computer that has been holding up well. I would recommend upgrading to an HDD hard drive to boost performance and speed if that is something that is important to you.

But it is REALLY annoying and spoils the experience of having an otherwise excellent piece of luggable technology. After searching I see key caps on Alienware's products are a problem are a problem for others, but I imagine some of that is because it can be a great gaming machine. I don't know if buying a replacement key-cap will solve the issue. I actually comes loose while the cover is down, not just from pressing it. Indeed the keyboard gets little use as my setup is such that I use a separate Logitech USB keyboard and mouse. But I need to use F9 and F10 on the laptop keyboard to adjust brightness.Original Review: Original rating still holds. I got this machine not for gaming but for remote on-location HD video production, editing, and rendering. Primary requirements were GPU and CPU performance and software compatibility. So far this machine has performed very well. I was concerned about and on the lookout for any issues with the display, critical in my work, that appeared in at least one review. I haven't yet seen any dead pixels. I needed a machine with an IPS display so that the screen could be viewed by more than one person, thus from oblique angles, with minimal darkening or color shift of the image. The display in the machine I received is excellent for my needs.There was a mention in one of the reviews about unsatisfactory color on the display. After considerable testing that is most certainly NOT THE CASE with the display in my machine. The display is excellent and color accurate. Read on. . . Consistency and accuracy of color, brightness, tonality, and nuance are critical in my professional work. I use a professional colorimeter-based display calibration system (DataColor's SPYDER product [ASIN:B00UBSL3L6 Datacolor Spyder5ELITE - Designed for Professional Photographers (S5EL100)] to calibrate all my displays on all my systems to the same viewing standard regardless of the hardware. This is a hardware and software solution to calibrate monitors on different systems to a fixed setting (determined by user requirements) so that the images displayed are as identical as possible. The precision colorimeter sensor measures the color output and brightness of the display across the full spectrum of displayable colors. The display in my Alienware laptop matches the displays on my large workstation monitors in a side-by-side comparison.I have run FurMark benchmarks on the machine, watching the CPU/GPU temp rise and then hearing the fans kick in. For a portable production system on a budget I think this will do the job. I'll update the review again if there are issues or Alienware/Dell steps up to this problem.

I've owned the ASUS ROG GL502VS-DB71 15.6" laptop for less than 6 months.  I've encountered no significant problems.All the complaints that others have posted are probably true, but they are also probably based on false expectations. Let me explain...Laptops and "gaming" machines are polar opposites. From the ground up, laptops are built for portability and battery life. If you pack them with "gaming" features (graphics card, CPU, RAM, etc) they start to become heavy, power hungry, run hot and burn battery fast. So laptops that stay on for a flight to Europe will not be able to run your games, and the ones that do will run out of juice in 1h (and burn your crotch in the process, assuming TSA lets you on the plane with that monster as a carryon.)As far as a compromise between the two opposite goals (laptop and gaming), this is a pretty good one.I have had an MSI i5? 17" system and a Razer i7 14" to compare it to. I am super happy that it doesn't run as hot as either of those two (which both broke in less than 24 months!). The Asus definitely has a "cheap" "plasticky" look to it compared to the Razer (which looked amazing, compact and polished as if cut out of 1 piece). Unfortunately, that compactness made for some poor cooling. This Asus seems to be more airy inside, and I haven't noticed it getting too-hot-to-touch. (it also has a better graphics card 1070 vs 970, while running the same games). Hopefully this will translate into more longevity.Pros1. (my MSI was 17" which was excessive, my Razer was 14" which was meh)2. not as hot as previous laptops I owned.Cons (all minor).1. some bloatware (can uninstall)2. cheap plastic look, esp the keyboard.3. headphones can easily pop out of the jack a fraction on an inch, switching to speakers.typical annoyances for gaming laptops...4. air vents downwards (I guess sideways and/or down are the only ways possible, but still annoying on your lap)5. DC transformer block is pretty large.6. typical gaming laptop battery life (1h gaming)

review_title: Okay Gaming Laptop with MAJOR Design Flaws
review_text: So I bought this laptop back in early 2017 (around the middle of January) and am still using it to this day (almost 2 years later). So take what I say with a decent amount of confidence and read my full review to understand why I'm giving this laptop such a low score even after 2 years of use. Go to the bottom for a TL;DR and list of pros and cons.So originally I was using a MSI GT72 Dominator laptop which I purchased back in 2015 and was using very regularly for school, work, and recreation. It just so happens that your younger sibling spilling coffee on the keyboard tends to ruin laptops. So I looked around and decided to acquire this laptop at it's very reasonable price tag of around 1,300 USD at the time of purchase. The nice slim design was really appealing for travel and to take back and forth to school and it had fairly decent reviews at the time (almost 4.5 stars). So I checked the full specs out online, benchmark scores, and tech reviews of the laptop. All of which indicated that it would be a decent buy. After receiving the laptop I used it for probably around 6 months without any issues whatsoever. Speeds were reasonably decent and it could run most anything (game wise) in medium-high settings without any issues. The on-board Wi-Fi adapter worked really well and I had no troubles with connectivity through that or while using a wired connection.The first noticeable issue came at about 7.5 months into using the laptop whenever the GPU fan started to make this awful grinding noise and it sounded like the fan was hitting the housing, something had gotten stuck in there, or a piece had come loose. So I opened up the laptop by removing the back panel and took out the fan to inspect it and saw no visual indication that anything was wrong. There was only minor dust buildup which I cleaned out and then reinstalled the fan into the computer. The problem was still there. So I went online and ordered another fan (which ran me about 40 USD with shipping) and installed that no problem. After about another month I started hearing the same noise coming from the other side of the computer. This time it was the CPU fan that was having the exact same problem. So I went ahead and did the same thing, visually inspected, cleaned it out, placed the part back, and checked that the connector wasn't damaged in any way. And yet, the problem was still there. So I ordered a CPU fan this time (roughly 30 USD with shipping) and replaced that as soon as it came in about a week later. No issues. Then about 4 months later the GPU AND the CPU fans both started having the issue again within about 4 days of one another, progressively getting worse and worse as more days went by. So this time I simply ordered 3 of each fan at a discounted rate and just have them on hand for the next time they fail.During all of this fan nonsense I started to notice performance drops in the read/write speed of the hard drive (which is not a very good hard drive to begin with). I had bought the model without the m.2 SSD installed and so it was VERY noticeable whenever the loading times on most apps/games and the write speeds to my external hard drive started to slow down tremendously (all the way down to almost 60MB/s write for single large files). So I went ahead and replaced my HDD with a Samsung 860 Evo 1TB SSD and had no further problems there. I eventually bought an enclosure for the HDD and use it as a storage for picture and low size media files as it's not very good for large sized data transfer. So just be forewarned that the HDD they use is a fairly cheap one and might not last the life of the computer.As far as RAM goes, if you buy the 16GB model it only comes with one stick, which is nice if you want to upgrade your RAM later on, but the performance on a single stick of RAM is absolutely shoddy compared to having two. Outside of specialized tasks, I really don't see why you would need more than 16GB in the first place. So keep that in mind if you plan on buying this PC.Now onto my biggest gripe with the computer. Cooling. This computer has the worst, and I do mean the worst, cooling setup I have ever seen out of all the laptops and desktops I have ever used. The amount of clearance (due to the slim factor) between the motherboard/fans and the bottom part of the case (where the fans draw air from) is horrific. You maybe have about a half inch, if even that, of clearance between where the lower part of the fan is and the desk where you'll likely be resting this computer on. On top of that the fans themselves are extremely small and can barely keep the internal parts cool enough for them to operate at maximum load during stress tests and while using extremely intensive applications and games. I found that my computer was suffering more from the CPU throttling due to temperatures than ANYTHING else during the entire time I've had this PC. I've played everything from the newest AAA games to the cheapest Steam games imaginable to intensive video editing software and beyond and the biggest hindrance through it all was the CPU throttling due to overheating because of the inadequate cooling setup for this laptop.TL;DR / SummaryThis is an okay laptop with decent specs and fairly modern hardware that can hold it's own for medium-high intensity games. The PC suffers a lot under intense use and has major overheating issues due to inadequate space for airflow because of the slim form factor of the laptop itself. The Hard Disk Drive that comes with the laptop is sub-par (cheap) and will probably need to be upgraded within 1-2 years of continuous use (less than 1 year if you're a very heavy user like myself). The RAM in the laptop comes in single 16GB stick format which causes it to under-preform when compared to a laptop with the same specs running two 8GB sticks at the same memory clock. This laptop has MAJOR issues with it's fans (more than likely due to the large strain put on them because of the design) and they will probably need to be replaced multiple times throughout the lifespan of the laptop (40 USD per GPU fan, 35 per CPU fan).*A thing to note with gaming laptops is that the battery generally will wear down quicker than a normal workstation style laptop and will hold less of a charge due to the higher power draw from the upgraded parts inside. This laptop is about average with it's battery life. Roughly 2-3 hours with light/minimal use. 1-1.5 with moderate use. And less than 1 with heavy/very intensive use.Pros:- Easy to travel with- Can run almost all modern games and new applications with ease in medium - high settings- Reasonably quiet unless running at full throttle- Average battery life for a gaming laptop- Comes in multiple configurations- Spare parts are easy to obtain for repairs- Very easy to upgradeCons:- MAJOR issues with cooling and fans- Slim design causes problems with airflow- Single RAM stick can cause issues when loading RAM intensive applications/games- HDD is cheap and WILL slow down quicker than a nice oneOverall I'd give this laptop an 6.5/10 with most of the drop in score coming from the cooling/fan issues. I personally wouldn't recommend this specific laptop or any ASUS laptop that has this same design to anyone looking to buy a gaming laptop. Try to find something similarly priced by Acer, MSI, or if you don't need a laptop then look to build your own desktop PC and get something like a Chromebook for mobile tasks (this is much cheaper than a gaming laptop). If you are set on getting a gaming laptop then make sure it's not a slim form factor to help with the cooling so that your parts (specifically the CPU) don't get throttled due to the temperature getting to high. I hope this helps inform anyone looking to buy this product. Have a great day!

review_title: it's not a bad laptop overall
review_text: I've had this laptop for about two weeks now. Having played around with it a bit and configured Windows 10 to what I want, it's not a bad laptop overall. It's not too heavy for me, seems well built and solid enough, and battery life, so far, has been running about 6-7 hours. I've had it on my lap for an hour or more at a time and it never gets beyond warm. Hard drive speed with the SSD (my first time using one) is fast, but I haven't really had to put the machine to work in order to detect just how much faster it is than a regular hard drive.The screen and keyboard are adequate (the keypad is a welcome for me as well). The key response is just enough to give you the feel that you've pressed the button; there is a light noiseless click when depressing keys, which I like. As to no keyboard backlighting, I don't care; I need an external source of light when I type, so I'm not bothered by that missing feature.The touchpad is apparently not an ELAN, so you can't run the Precision software Microsoft puts out for that, which I would rather use than the ASUS Gestures - it's not as fine-tuning as it should be, but it works.Battery Health Charger (software that enables better battery longevity) does not come with this laptop, and the software (which is downloadable) will not work when installed after the fact. This confirmed by ASUS after I couldn't get it to work.As for graphics, you cannot disable the integrated Intel graphics processor (HD 620, I believe it is) in order to just run the NVIDIA 940 - bios options do not support this option, and disabling the Intel driver in the Device Manager disables both drivers. Thus, it seems the only way to kick in the NVIDIA driver is to use its control panel to set it to run with the particular software you wish, if you can find it listed and available to do so. Otherwise, the Intel on-board is a good processor and will do just fine for general all-around graphics processing, which is all I need.By the way, it is because of the touchpad, battery and graphics shortcomings I've noted above that I've given the laptop 4 instead of 5 stars.As to wifi, download speeds, this, that and the other related features, I've paid little attention to those matters because it's not that important for me. I will be using this machine pretty much just for Internet research, writing, some YouTube and other minor program running. (This machine will be taking over for my desktop, which I will upgrade and use for what few games I play, for photography post processing and for composing music - much bigger and nicer monitor on the desktop!)The problems that I've come across have been Windows issues, I'm sure (confirmed after doing some research on the Net): battery icon disappears and the speaker icon doesn't do anything when clicking on it. At the moment, both, however, are working. For the battery, the fix was to uninstall the battery drivers in Device Manager and rescan the hardware (one driver at a time). For the speakers, it's a matter of either using the fn-F11/12 keys (volume control) or restarting Windows Explorer through the Task Manager. Both fixes, I don't believe, are machine related, and I'm still testing these "fixes" to see if the battery and speaker icons will stay fixed. (Doing so as I write.)So overall, I'm quite pleased with the machine. I tried to find a lower performance machine for a few hundred dollars cheaper that got equally good reviews as this one but simply couldn't find what made me feel comfortable in the purchase. So, I dropped a grand on this one. It's got to last me a good 5-7 years, I hope, to make the investment well worth it. We will see.

review_title: A personally fitting laptop with a reasonable price tag
review_text:
HP ENVY 13-ab016nr Notebook (Intel Core i5-7200U, 8GB RAM, 256GB SSD) with Windows 10









  
  
    
  To give a little background, I pre-ordered this laptop after doing a sizable amount of research on several different laptops that fit my general needs and it arrived on the 15th of November (I've had it for about two weeks now). My brother owns the HP-Spectre 2-in-1 and a couple of friends own older models of the HP-ENVY-15. The large majority of my friends have MacBooks. That being said, these are the machines I will be comparing it to in order to give a general feel for the laptop. Sorry for the long review, but since the product is new I'd like to give my own personal opinion that isn't a "get a free product to give us 5 stars" type of review.Starting at the price of $700 (I bought it for $750 actually), it is more than half that of a MacBook Pro and slightly more than half a MacBook (2016 models) and also cheaper or the same price as OLDER ENVY-13 models on amazon. At this price point, you are getting the standard 8GB of RAM with a 256GB SSD (a must in my book). The HP Spectre offers a 128GB SSD at a price point of $999 new at the time of this review. This ENVY 13 also has the newest 7th generation i5-7200U, and while it's not a quad-core CPU, that wasn't what I was looking for in a laptop. For browsing and medium media consumption, it will work just fine, and it has a slight edge over older models of the ENVY and the spectre which are running 6th generation processors. For context, I streamed 4K video from YouTube to my 50-inch 1080p TV through HDMI, and though the area where the processor lies (right above the keyboard, P.S. the fans release right under the bottom bezel [which is quite large]) was quite hot, it managed to keep going and produce constant video. Port wise, this machine overs more than sufficient connections and will probably last me a good while without the need for a port. In case the description/picture don't give you a good view... on the left you have a microSD card slot, USB type C, and headphone jack. On the right, the power cord slot lies with the HDMI, and two USB 3.1's. As a rule of thumb, battery life listed is always going to be the best they can possible sap from it. 14 hours is like lowest brightness with minimal usage. My personal estimate from daily use is 4-6 hours of constant work/play and anywhere from 7-10 with more moderate usage on a reasonable brightness setting with the only time I ever really got even the HP battery estimate over 10 hours was quite literally lowest brightness setting and I just left the laptop sitting (again these are more estimates than fact, and so far the laptop hasn't died on me before I was able to get to my charger). The design on the ENVY 13 is stellar, rocking the new HP logo, a nice backlit keyboard that I personally prefer over my friends' macbooks, and a sleek form factor. However, I will say the build quality is sub-par to the macbook, which I garnered as much since I still think MacBooks are the golden standard for build quality. For example, the bezel on the screen isn't great, and there is a good deal of flex in the screen. In addition, the hinge is wobbly, and while it won't jiggle while typing or moving the laptop, it doesn't seem the sturdiest. Since the laptop has only been available for 2-3 weeks, I doubt any reviews as of now can tell you if it lasted very long yet (my bet is that if anything, the hinge will start to deteriorate and I've heard the same problems that existed in the 2015 model are still present in this one, just better looking). However, I do appreciate the almost all aluminum (or at least I think it is aluminum) brushed finish. Overall, the small body, relative light weight, and ease of carrying in my backpack while still having enough horsepower make it ideal for me personally.Aside from the build quality, my biggest complaint would have to be the trackpad. Comparing it to even the spectre, this thing is tiny. Not tiny to the point of unusable, but it's smaller than most I've seen (I don't think this is a good thing, but maybe you might). The tracking isn't great, I find it backpeddling from time to time for some reason. Also, periodically it seems to phantom click (I don't know the best way to describe this, but at times I can be hovering whilst not clicking, but it registers a click). This isn't super frequent, but it happens enough to be noticeable. If you're use to a MacBook's trackpad, this will be a step-down for sure.Again, if you're not a huge iOS guy and you want to save quite literally another $600-900, this is a fine replacement. The HP ENVY 15 is more or less the same, and might provide slightly better specs for less money, but the clunkiness and aesthetic was not for me. A convertible and/or the ability for a touchscreen wasn't enough for me to sacrifice storage and performance for an otherwise more expensive and even less durable design in the Spectre (but it does look amazing, I will give it that).

review_title: Powerful and stylish, you won't find a better laptop in this price range.
review_text: After researching laptops for the past 3 months, I decided to go with the HP Envy 13, and I'm really glad I did.I wanted something that was powerful enough to run Photoshop and Illustrator, as well as something that I could code on and this machine fits the bill.  The Kaby Lake core i5 processor (the latest generation chip) coupled with 8 GB of RAM really makes this thing fly.  The 1920x1080 pixel screen has a great color profile with decent contrast, and is one of the best screens I've seen in a sub $600 laptop, and images are vivid and crisp on this beautifully bright IPS panel.  I've had no issues with overheating or a loud fan as some people have noted, and I've put it through its paces.The build quality on this is awesome, with it's all aluminum body.  Very solid and feels good to carry around.  It's also a very stylish, attractive machine that rivals the design of a macbook.  It's also very easy to type on this (which was a big selling point for meThe solid state drive in this thing enables Windows to boot in under 8 seconds, and it has a very high read/write speed.The touchpad is very responsive and a pleasure to use, handling Windows 10 gestures perfectly, making web surfing a breeze.Battery life is great, and I've averaged about 8-9 hours on a charge, and this machine charges fast too... I've gotten a full charge from 5% to 100% in about an hour and a half.Overall I'm very pleased with this purchase, and would recommend it to anyone looking to buy an affordable ultraportable laptop.  Fast, stylish and a great screen makes this machine a pure gem.  Don't hesitate to purchase it, I'd definitely buy it again.

I am about to start school in August for an Electrical Engineering degree and have a decent background with building my own PC's.When you buy a laptop it's very important to look at EVERY aspect of it's performance since you'll likely be unable or unwilling to upgrade the internal parts later without a lot of unnecessary hassle. That being said here are the things I love about this laptop,256GB Storage space: Admittedly this isn't the BEST in the market, however considering how thin and attractive this PC is and the price point, i'm very happy with it. BONUS: ALL of the memory on this pc is SSD storage which means increased performance and cooler/quieter running.8GB of RAM: I run Photoshop for my personal/professional life. so having the extra RAM to process all my brushstrokes and effects makes this a MUST. anything 4 and under just doesn't cut it if you have lengthy projects to work on.Intel Core i5-7200U: Again another category where you get the best of both worlds, this is both inexpensive and performs well on many benchmarks. It's no powerhouse for gaming mind you, but it'll do the job all the same and give you little trouble.I also get minimal stuttering from Heroes of the stormThe keyboard feels soft but responsive and is quiet, plus the backlight is nice.I also like the trackpad, multitouch gestures, smooth surface that doesn't lend to gathering oily junk.The battery is O.K. it's not some megahouse but it's enough to get the job done if you're moving from point A- to point B (Besides who doesn't travel without their cable anyway)I made sure to wipe the OS with a fresh install immedietly after purchase and I notice both a performance and battery boost.Overall rating: I will need more time and will possibly update my review after about a month or two, however I really REALLY enjoy the laptop so  far, it's light, responsive, quiet and sexy.Would recommend for price/performance B+

Overall, the hardware is absolutely incredible.In terms of battery life, if you have the proper power plan in place (which you will have to change in the Dragon Center app), I get around 4 hours of battery. This is with the keyboard turned down as dim as possible and the screen also very dim. The laptop also uses the Intel HD Graphics when not plugged in, so it prolongs the battery life even more. I was super pleased by this, as I expected it to be much less!Now, here's where things get hairy: bloatware and updates. This is what I mentioned above when I said you need to know what you're doing. First of all, as soon as you set up this laptop, head straight to the control panel and uninstall Norton and all the bloatware (such as the Magix stuff.) All this software does is run at startup and slowdown your PC, as well as decrease battery life. However, absolutely do not uninstall Dragon Center, Steelseries Engine 3, and SCM, as these are essential to controlling your PC. After all this is done, download the Intel Driver Update Utility and update your chipset and Intel graphics driver! This will also give you longer battery life. Finally, update the Nvidia drivers, and you should be good to go!I didn't fault the laptop on this, as all laptop manufacturers do this. They are paid to put certain software on their computers by companies, and I've  come to expect it.All in all, I am simply stunned. This laptop is wonderful, and I'm super happy with it! If you know how to use a computer properly, it will pay dividends for you.Thanks for reading my review, and I hoped it helped!

review_title: Loved this laptop, but motherboard died after 3 years
review_text: This was a great laptop.  My work is 100% remote, with occasional travel.  This laptop gave me the power and speed that exceeds the desktop PCs my company issues, with the flexibility to use only one device that I can pick up and carry with me when I am on-call or have to travel.  I run multiple VMs, including Oracle and MSSQL databases, and also use multiple VPNs & softphones, group collaboration & remote control apps.  I've rarely had a problem with voice / video degradation, even when running three or four guest VMs with Server operating systems.  The Samsung 950Pro NVMe drive I added results in faster IOPS than most of my customer's production databases.  Sometimes, I can take a backup copy of a database and actually run intensive database operations on this laptop faster than they run on customer's production servers.But, after 3.2 years of 50-70 hours/wk constant use, the motherboard died.  Used replacement motherboard / CPU combinations are more expensive than a refurb laptop, unless ordered from China and wait for weeks.The main downside, other than short life, was the battery run time was only about an hour or so, but it was enough for my purposes.

review_title: This was just fine with me for $400 off of the normal retail ...
review_text: I purchased this machine from a third party (Mobile Advance) through Amazon, used. The description of the product said that there was a "scratch," and I assumed they meant on the laptop's chassis itself. This was just fine with me for $400 off of the normal retail price. But no! I got a pleasant surprise when it arrived. The scratch was on the BOX, which had clearly been through some minor wear and tear. The laptop itself was in pristine condition; I could not have asked for better if I had bought it directly from the manufacturer.And the machine itself is exactly what I need. The design is streamlined and nice to look at. Heavy, of course, but when closed it is not too awkward to carry. I bought this computer to game, and though I am by no means a hardcore PC gamer, I like the experience to be immersive no matter what I'm playing. And for what I enjoy (Assassin's Creed, Skyrim, The Sims 4) it certainly is. Skyrim can be played with zero lag on Advanced quality and on Ultra quality with lag during large battle scenes, all DLC included. The screen is large enough that I forget I'm not on a desktop. The keyboard is satisfying crisp with each keystroke. I can now type at my full speed since this laptop will not be confused by multiple keys being hit very quickly. I no longer have to patiently fiddle with quality settings so that I don't wait for eons for things to load. I can now just enjoy movies, TV shows, and take care of my e-mail no problem.Overall, I would say that if you like to play moderately demanding games (or games that were high-end at the time of their release) in an immersive way without worries, this would be an ideal machine. I can also confidently recommend Mobile Advance as a third-party seller, who I thank for making this nerve-wracking buying experience of a first budget gaming laptop so great!

review_title: Used to be a hardcore HP Fan now a Asus Fan
review_text: There is no better laptop in my opinion.  I actually bought a second one in 2017 after I passed this one to my husband.  The new solid state hard drive is awesome

The MSI GS63VR 15.6" with 4K display is a nice upgrade from the GS60 predecessor.LOOK/FEEL: It now has an Mg-Li chassis which feels pretty darn metal and is better built than the original Barbie plastic, although it can be a fingerprint magnet. The screen bezel has been reduced from the Hugh Mungus one the GS60 had to a slimmer one, so that's a nice detail. The power button has been moved to the side with a smaller, more compact and low-key button, which is an improvement over the previous blue ring of blinding light. At first I pressed the power button on accident causing the computer to go to sleep mode and some memes to be left un-shown, but I quickly got used to not picking it up as such. The keyboard is great, with some nice key travel and the island-style keys are very tropical to use. There's also a cloth laminate on the bottom to help the laptop not cause you long-term infertility. The 4k screen is very crisp and has good viewing angles, although be wary of some programs (AutoCAD, Sketchup) not scaling well because they have not been optimized for such a resolution, which can result in a very interesting collage of differing font sizes and UI's for ants (you can always switch to 1080p and have no problems). The trackpad also feels nice, but you're going to use a mouse anyway. Overall, the laptop is a tad more compact than the previous model and feels way better built. I also like the fact that it doesn't have the tacky gamer aesthetic that most laptops of its kind seem to have. It's sleek af.PERFORMANCE: This thing runs. Very well. The new GTX 1060 offers a huge improvement over the previous 970. Games like Overwatch, Witcher 3, Metal Gear Solid V, etc. run smooth as butter on very-high/ultra (they do not dip below 60FPS). When playing Overwatch, my temps run at ~60C which are way better than the previous model (~76 C). You'll be able to caress the most demanding and future titles with much needed TLC. Note: I had to mess with the GeForce Experience to disable the in-game overlay they force down your throat, and uninstalled some unnecessary programs first (*note some reviews describing a problem with the stuttering, which is a problem caused by this from my experience). To be fair, though, the Experience thing is a flaw from Nvidia, not this laptop. After that, it was smooth sailing. Buy a laptop fan stand to keep temps down (this applies to any gaming computer). Also, no G-Sync (why?) which is kind of a downer for those using external 144hz monitors considering this thing can pump more than 60FPS on most games, but this is something extra and you'd have to get at least 120 fps on high-end games for you to be able to notice a difference.STORAGE: The 512GB SSD runs fast and makes my system boot up fast enough for me to pick the laptop up and use it right away. The HDD is slow as hell compared to the SSD, so use it for storage only. This is not really an issue for me since the 512 GB of storage is enough to let you install all the apps and games there with no issues. If it was 256 gigs, it would be a different story. You can always replace the HDD for an SSD without worrying about voiding the warranty.PORTS: 3 USB 3.0's, which is enough. A DisplayPort and an HDMI cable. Standard Headphone/Mic inputs. The Ethernet and SD slot are convenient. Oh. There's an extra USB 2.0 port if you want to get schwifty with the cavemen, or you know...want to use it for a mouse or keyboard.BATTERY: Battery life is good. Lasted me more than 4 hours on Battery saving mode while doing some light work and studying some powerpoints. For a gaming laptop, this is not bad at all in my opinion. You really can't expect more for the perfomance, and expect the battery to not last more than 2 hours under heavy load. The charger is a bit smaller than the previous model, but it's still good for self-defense. :)VALUE: (I have added this section for people looking for more bang for the buck) Compared to the build quality of other laptops in the same range (Gigabyte, Asus Strix, Razer Blade), I would say it is a good amount of value, considering you get better temps, storage, display and dedicated graphics than a similar Blade ($2200). The Blade is a tad more portable. The Asus Strix / Gigabyte P57 has a better video card (1070 over 1060), however falling short of this laptop with the build quality, so if you don't care for that and prefer value and a bit better peformance, go with that one. This laptop is more middle-of-the-road in terms of balance between specs and design.Overall, this is a nice boost in quality. Runs well, looks good. Despite its few flaws, it is a very well-built laptop with specs to keep you on the extreme, Dorito-munching, Mountain Dew-drinking gaming groove. After some uninstalling of software (you can just do a fresh install of windows too), the micro-stuttering issue was gone. Definitely recommend.UPDATE: In my experience, the Windows 10 Anniversary Edition update has fixed a problem is also started having considering turning off the laptop when connected to an external monitor. I no longer have this issue. So far, the laptop runs great with no issues whatsoever.

If you pack them with "gaming" features (graphics card, CPU, RAM, etc) they start to become heavy, power hungry, run hot and burn battery fast. So laptops that stay on for a flight to Europe will not be able to run your games, and the ones that do will run out of juice in 1h (and burn your crotch in the process, assuming TSA lets you on the plane with that monster as a carryon.)As far as a compromise between the two opposite goals (laptop and gaming), this is a pretty good one.I have had an MSI i5? 17" system and a Razer i7 14" to compare it to. I am super happy that it doesn't run as hot as either of those two (which both broke in less than 24 months!). The Asus definitely has a "cheap" "plasticky" look to it compared to the Razer (which looked amazing, compact and polished as if cut out of 1 piece). Unfortunately, that compactness made for some poor cooling. This Asus seems to be more airy inside, and I haven't noticed it getting too-hot-to-touch. (it also has a better graphics card 1070 vs 970, while running the same games). Hopefully this will translate into more longevity.Pros1. I haven't though 15.6" of screen is "big" since the 90s, but it sure is nice on a laptop. (my MSI was 17" which was excessive, my Razer was 14" which was meh)2. not as hot as previous laptops I owned.Cons (all minor).1. some bloatware (can uninstall)2. cheap plastic look, esp the keyboard.3. headphones can easily pop out of the jack a fraction on an inch, switching to speakers.typical annoyances for gaming laptops...4. air vents downwards (I guess sideways and/or down are the only ways possible, but still annoying on your lap)5. DC transformer block is pretty large.6. typical gaming laptop battery life (1h gaming)

review_title: ... once counseled us to never get the latest and greatest laptops, since there would always be a heating ...

After trying an HP laptop that refused to work with corporate standard software (RSA SecurID Token), I finally decided to get this sweet baby as an "away-from-home" game and work computer.  After replacing the (more than adequate) 7200 RPM hard drive with a 1 TB SSD, I'm liking this beast better and better.  (there is a second M.2 slot nobody mentioned).  It's heaver than I first hoped, and I'm no fan of the chiclet keys, but everything else is pretty great about it, and I DO need the exercise! ;)I would rate it a 4.5 because the m.2 SSD boot drive is not visible from the recovery disk of Acronis True Image 2016, forcing me to backup using Microsoft's backup solution, which has the unfortunate limitation of demanding to use the top-level directory of their back-up device rather than a sub-directory.  I haven't tried to restore Windows using Microsoft's backup software, while I've had Acronis software save my hash multiple times.  Maybe the next version of Acronis will be able to see it, and I'll have better peace of mind.

review_title: Beautiful performance - until it no longer works...
review_text: I've owned this computer for approximately 17 months, using it primarily to manage my music collection and play occasional games (Civilization series or Total War) during Christmas and Spring Breaks with my 17 year old son. Instead, I'm now faced with a very hefty repair bill for a blown motherboard.To be fair, Asus has a policy and they are simply following it.  I respect their decision to do so. I've explained all of this to Asus and they waived return shipping and 1/2 the labor costs for me.  While I appreciate a lower bill, it is not even 10% of the repair costs overall.Again, they have every right to follow their policy just as I have every right to post this review.  I'm simply disappointed in their choice to follow policy to the letter rather than take the opportunity to prove to a loyal customer that I've been making good choices all these years.  Based on what has happened, I will not be buying Asus computers in the future. review_title: Capable of demanding tasks. Not a mainstream machine.
review_text: I bought this laptop a few days ago and have been using it everyday since. This is a major upgrade from my previous laptop which was 4 years old. I'm a software engineer so speed is critically important to me, and so far this machine has what I need. Still waiting on installing the SSD, but so far no complaint whatsoever performance-wise.Design-wise, this is a tad heavy compared to the Macbook Pro 15'', and feels a bit clunky due to the weight. This laptop wouldn't be something I'd carry around in my bag. I have been using it at home, plugged in (the battery life is hilariously short) 100%, so mobility isn't a concern for me. If you are used to the Mac and want mobility, then you might want to reconsider this laptop. Having said that, it is fine if you want to put it on your laps.The backlit keyboard is great. Before the purchase I was a bit concerned by the color red, but now that I see it in person, it isn't something annoying. You can change the brightness of the backlight depending on your surrounding lighting. I usually have it up at 75% to max. The keys themselves are great - I can type really fast with them thanks to the positioning and the responsiveness. Before buying this laptop, I did all my programming/coding work on the Mac and I loved its keyboard. The ASUS ROG's keyboard doesn't disappoint me in any bit. However, this laptop has the number pad to the right and I feel that isn't necessary.The touchpad: It isn't as bad as other people have said. Again, I'm comparing it directly with the Macbook Pro's touchpad I use everyday for work, and this ROG machine's touchpad provides a very similar experience. You can quickly scroll up and down, show all opening programs, do a two-finger tap to trigger the right-click option, etc. These are controlled by and can be disabled in the ASUS Smart Gesture program that comes with the laptop. The only strange thing about the touchpad is that it isn't positioned at the center of the keyboard, but more towards the left. I always find myself having to reach a little bit more for the left-click, but over time this should be second-nature to me. Again, nothing fancy - it's a touchpad that works and is decently responsive. I seriously don't get why other people complained about the touchpad.The battery life is outrageously short, and I think this counts heavily against the machine. I have been using this laptop plugged in 100% of the time if this is a deal breaker for some. Somehow the computer still burns its juice in sleep mode, so if you leave your laptop sleeping overnight on battery, it will go from 100% to roughly 10% the next morning when you wake it up. Normal usage on battery will give you roughly 1 hour or more, which is shockingly short. If you plug in and start gaming away, by the time you are done with your games, the battery will have only increased a bare single-digit %. In other words, having to plug in, coupled with the weight of the machine, reduces mobility. If you only need a laptop that lasts long enough, then this isn't the right model for you.The screen's brightness leaves room to be desired. I found out you can turn it further up via the Intel HD Graphics tool that came with the laptop. However, it is matte black so there is no glare whatsoever, and it supports viewing from a lot of different angles. There is a CD/DVD tray that I don't need so this part is unnecessary. Interestingly there is a USB-C port for those using USB-C devices but I haven't use this port. Audio is really bad (not high quality, and doesn't get very loud) so you need a line out to your speakers or headphones to enjoy the sound.I uninstalled most of the software that ships with the laptop (mostly ASUS stuff, Office, and McAfee). The hardware is as listed here on Amazon for the DH71, 15", model. To summarize: Intel i7 processor, 16 GB of RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960M, Intel HD Graphics, 1 TB HDD. Booting the machine out of the box was smooth and easy. I encountered no problem at all (yep, not a single one). I upgraded BIOS, and let Windows 10 update itself, which took several hours and several restarts. The NVIDIA software also needed updates. In short, things went as smooth as can be.Now I have installed Android Studio (and several GBs of the Android SDK - simulators run a bit slow but I tend to run apps from my physical phones), Visual Studio, BitDefender as my antivirus, PowerDVD, K Lite Mega Codecs, and a few other games and programs. No performance bottleneck that I have seen so far, running off of the HDD. I will try to install the SSD and migrate my programs over the new drive, though. Boot time to Windows is very sweet - around 10 seconds not counting a few more seconds to log you in.This laptop is ideal if you care a lot about performance, speed, and if you are a gamer. I bought this machine for my software engineering tasks that I normally do on my $2K Macbook Pro. This machine is not for your casual work like checking emails, playing music, and browsing the web. At 100%, the text are still sharp and legible, but wouldn't recommend it as it would strain your eyes. Obviously, your mileage will vary depending on your eyes.The only downside is the price, this is a pricey machine, but it's really nice.

review_text: If you're reading this review it's because you're in the marketplace to buy a new puter running the latest i5 CPU or killing time. Well, read on. The higher rating means better performance.This i5 rocks over an i3.Memory  DDR4 - 4 *****Kingston PC-2400R, one 8 GB stick.SSD - NoneSK Hynix M.2 SATA III 256 GB - 5 *****Surprised to discover my rig is running with an M.2 SATA III stick instead of an SSD. The SSD hole is empty in case one wishes to add one. It's not PCI-e so you won't notice the difference in speed between this M.2 and an SSD. In a year or two I expect to see laptops with PCI-e capable M.2 sticks which will be capable of up to 32 GB speeds vs the 6GB SATA III speed.GPU Nvidea GeForce 940MXThis GPU is sick! Please note an unknown Intel GPU also comes with the unit. The GPU is where you set brightness AND contrast. You do this by right clicking an empty spot on your desktop, the drop down menu will list Intel Graphics Setting and Nvidea Control Panel. Set every control to the Nvidea card; 3D and PhysX, brightness, contrast, hue and saturation. The system is set to auto select between the two but appears to always choose the crappy fuzzy Intel GPU. I imagine the Intel GPU is what drives i3 machines. I can't tell you enough how horrible the Intel GPU makes the display look. Once set for Nvidea the display comes to life, letters are crisp and sharp, and colors vibrant. Display speed and screen refresh is speedy too.Display - 5 *****Glossy screens are very reflective. Looks cool but who wants glare, who wants a screen that resembles a mirror? Not me. This matte screen is very anti-reflective yet at the same time very sharp/detailed, as long as you set GPU control to Nvidea (see GPU comments above). This display has zero glare, zero reflection even with a reading lamp above and behind my shoulder pointing directly at the screen or sitting in front of a bay window with mid-day sun. And, no, I haven't taken the laptop outside. I will update later when It stops raining.Keyboard and Touchpad - 4.5 *****Keyboard key strokes are very good, not the best. Still very good for the buck$. Love that it comes with a numeric keypad. And that it has a backlight!Touchpad works great with no L/R buttons. Just press anywhere on the left or right side for it to function. It's quite obvious the 1 * reviewer is a NOOB or an agent of another mfg.Hardware - 5 *****Love that Acer didn't cheapen the machine by leaving out hardware. It's nice to have DVD R/W, Ethernet  rj-45  port, HDMI and VGA outputs, an SD card slot, headphone jack, and 3 USB ports two of which are 3.0. There's an odd hole on the left side near the screen. Since the machine did not come with a owner/user manual who knows what this hole is for. Perhaps for a cable lock for business security?Cosmetics - 5 *****I love the brushed black look.Other StuffVery minimal bloatware. Used Revo Uninstaller to remove trial crap.Surface smudges are minimal and wipes off easily.Power cord has right angle swivel plug. And cord from adapter to laptop is 6' long.Battery does last 11+ hours. And, laptop comes with battery life indicator icon located in the taskbar.Weight is heavy attributed to the long battery life. I'll sacrifice weight when I get hot performance.Is the battery user removable? Unknown for now as the back cover has to be removed. And my searches have not turned any replacement batteries for sale. In a few years I anticipate the market will be flooded with replacement batteries. I can uninstall/install any battery so no sweat of my brow when it comes time to do so.***UPDATE*** 12.10.2016I have noticed two buggy quirks; one irritating, the other nonsense1. Touchpad scrolling direction cannot be changed. Settings>Devices> Mouse & touchpad> Reverse scrolling direction set On or Off doesn't work. To see the lower portion of a page you slide your fingers towards the keyboard, away from the keyboard to see upper portion of a page. This is set and cannot be changed.2. Font size changes unexpectedly, usually smaller, lighter with squigly lettering. This makes them barely legible. Happens with Firefox, IE & Chrome. Close & reopen the browser and/or App resolves the problem. Arrrgh!*** UPDATE *** 01.07.2017Wierd mechanical break-in period1. The font size changing on its own has stopped. Dunno why but it did and I'm happy.2. The touchpad lef/right action will only work on the bottom corners.. There's a setting for this which I unticked. At first it allowed me to use the left/right edges of the touchpad, now only the bottom corners.3. Battery is user replaceable. Remove the 15 case screws and a couple  under the case and you'll find the battery near the screen.Be sure to pull out the DVD drive prior to case removing.  Pull gently on the small plug and, wala,  the battery comes out. Piece of cake.

After much research and review checking, I purchased this notebook for my sister to replace the aging and decrepit (Core 2 Duo) iMac she was using. This laptop is incredible, and I'm honestly very envious of my sister. I actually gave her the choice of my 11-inch MacBook Air or the new Dell laptop. She went with the Dell, and I both applaud and lament her good sense.First of all, this laptop came with ZERO BLOATWARE installed. It was a clean Windows 10 "Signature Edition" install which I'm guessing is why there were no unneeded (and unwanted) programs, demos, and trials. The only item I uninstalled was the "Get Office" placeholder app since she already had an Office license from her old machinewhich was running Win7 (her preference).The form factor is, frankly, mind-blowing. The bezel is all but nonexistent, and because of this the "13-inch" laptop is only a shred wider and longer than my "11-inch" MacBook Air. If I were to compare it to a 13-inch Air, it would be comical. See included photos. And gape in astonishment.As far as performance goes, the laptop is solid. Its integrated Intel HD 520 graphics can run my sister's Battle.net games just fine. Yes, she has them on low settings, but this is not a gaming rigit's a laptop, and a very slim and compact one. For playing Heroes of the Storm or Overwatch on the go, it certainly does the job.I think the only "problem" is the placement of the webcam in the lower corner of the bezel (but where else would you fit it?), since it basically looks up at you instead of forward. If you like to use Skype or Hangouts to video chat, the angle may look a little odd.The 8GB of RAM are plenty for almost any application for which you'd use this sort of laptop. The 128GB internal drive, however, is much smaller than I'd prefer. Had my sister chosen the Apple laptop, I'd have undoubtely ended up buying a larger M.2 drive and installing it in the Dell for my own use. Boom:

  
SanDisk SD8SN8U-1T00-1122 X400 M.2 SSD 1TB









  
  
    
  The screen is "only" 1920x1080 pixels (aka 1080p). However, for a 13" screen, I find that this is plenty. Any more pixels, and you're going to need to adjust scaling for visibility, anyway. It would also be significantly more taxing on the system to try to drive, say, a 4K display. Could it be done? Yeah, certainly. review_title: great laptop but has quality issues
review_text: I bought this laptop about a month ago and am very pleased.  My needs are not very demanding but there are times when I need the power of a game PC.  The desktop graphics are smooth and without hesitation.  The machine has more than enough power to attach an HDMI TV, extend the desktop to it and watch a DVD on one while using the other half for other things.  The fans in my other non-gaming laptops would be roaring to keep them cool before eventually overheating.  This Asus, however, doesn't break a sweat.  It's very quiet even when the CPU is stressed.  I've played a few games, and the graphics are incredibly smooth, and the machine is very responsive to the keyboard and game controllers.When editing photos and videos, it handles the large volumes of image data like a champ.It crunches through large computational Excel spreadsheets in a fraction of the time as my 8 year old Dell Vostro 1700.There are a few minor quirks.  The touchpad is very large.  Small hands will have trouble typing without accidentally touching it.  My adult hands are of average size, but they still sometimes accidentally touch it, and this causes the cursor and focus to unexpectedly jump elsewhere.  The numlock doesn't stay when the PC is shutdown. It will stay when hibernated.  The red on black keyboard lettering is not easily visible, even when the keyboard is back light is on.  I would have preferred the usual white on black lettering.  Occasionally, when the screen blanks to conserve power it can't be reactivated despite the machine being awake.  One work-around is to press fn-F1 which hibernates the machine and then immediately awaken it by pressing any key.  There don't seem to be any side-effects.Compared to my old Dell Vostro 1700, also a 17" screen, the Asus is an inch larger in width and length and will not fit inside my backpack which itself is large.  The power adapter is also quite large and heavy.  The laptop and power adapter combined must weight about 13 pounds.It's a solid laptop.  The only thing more that I could ask for is a 4K display.4/1/18 - updateAfter owning this laptop about a year, I'm downgrading the rating to 3 stars.  Perhaps I got a lemon, but the laptop has been sent to Asus 3 times for servicing.  The first time was to fix a power-on issue, where it would not power-on or its display would be remain black.  It would also lose WiFi connection after a couple hours.  It was with Asus for almost a month while parts were ordered.  The second time was to fix the same power-on issue and replace the optical drive because it would not write on DVD+R DL media.  The third time (currently) is to fix the num-lock indicator light which stopped working after the second repair.  Additionally, the laptop case was damaged upon arrival at Asus, so it took a couple days to resolve this too.  It has been two weeks, and I hope it will be returned to me this week.

review_title: A lightweight laptop for lightweight duties.
review_text: Let's get this out of the way first - no, it won't play Fortnite. No, it won't play Apex Legends. Plays a mean game of Angry Birds, though. However, if you just need a simple, lightweight laptop for email, web browsing or to transfer your porn collection to a USB drive, this is fine. It's a fairly stylish looking machine. Lightweight, with a somewhat cheap-feeling build, but good enough. The keyboard is actually rather nice, while the mousepad is semi-responsive (definitely get yourself a cheap mouse along with the laptop).  Obviously storage is an issue, but you can run programs from USB drives, so you're definitely going to need some extra storage. I have several 64gb 'thumb drives', and have been running apps from them with no issue whatsoever.  Also, there's a fair amount of bloatware included in the package, so if you jettison that, you'll retrieve a fair amount of onboard storage.  You can actually push this little laptop further than you might think. I've downloaded a couple of games (Doki Doki Literature Club, the old Westwood Blade Runner adventure game) plus some streaming software (XSplit Broadcaster) and managed to live stream these games to YouTube with no issues. Obviously, neither of these is graphically intensive, but I was still surprised that it managed to run a game, streaming software AND stream in 720p to YouTube without a hitch. It has two USB 2.0 ports, one USB 3.0 port, an SD Card slot, which will also take Micro SD cards with an adapter (usually included when you buy a Micro SD card), headphone jack port, and an HDMI Out port. No ethernet port, so you're going to be connecting to the internet via Wi-Fi, or not at all.  Basically, if you just need a cute little travel laptop for light duties, and you absolutely must have a Windows machine, as opposed to a Chromebook, then this is a decent choice. It won't blow you away with performance or build quality, but you're probably not going to feel ripped-off, either.
