review_title: Unbelievable, the new standard is this laptop
review_text: Unbelievable, powerhouse in 1 kg with big 15.6" screen, best laptop ever!Exceptional machine.Everybody is going for Surface Pros, Surface Books and MacBook Pros. They all weight at least 50% more taking into consideration the screen size. I worked with a Sony Z, 13.3" ~920 grams, this LG is even better , also Surface pro 3, all good machines, but this LG surpasses them overall. Unfortunately Lenovo has remained behind regarding portability, loved their machines but they are too heavy now.So, if you need a no-compromise machine with a big screen and extremely portable, this is it.21st century computer, only 1080 grams for a 15" screen and top of the range specs.Granted that the screen is not 4k, Don't see why anybody would need 4k for work. Especially because Windows does scaling (a sort of zoom) to make the icons and text readable because they would be too small, but in business applications this does not apply well and you see blurry content. Also if you connect the 4k laptop to a Full-HD screen, the scaling applies on the second monitor as well, extremely irritating (maybe they improved this in Win10?).The design is cool, I don't like bling and shiny stuff, this laptop is simple and elegant. The body does not flex even if it is so slim, the screen flexes quite a bit, received half-witted comments from technical reviews for that. LG has publish that this is by design, in order to make the screen resistant to falls and shocks. they have a video to prove it. Anyway shouldn't be bothered by it. Also that screen does not have the brightness of the Surface Pro 3 for example, but for me it's enough. I work at home or at the office, so there's no bother.Before I bought it, I read some comments that it feels like cheap plastic even if it is of magnesium, now I can say it's fine. I never buy devices for unibody design and stuff like that, I like function.I don't actually know why anybody would buy something else, this laptop is the new standard, everybody else (Microsoft, Apple, HP, DELL) all make noise for nothing, their comparable machines have 2 kg for same specs.PS:I am so baffled, this product is the new standard and no main top ten ultrabook reviews mention it, it confirms to me that every big tech publication's reviews are paid. This product so blows the competition away.

I really wanted to love this laptop - it is THE lightest 15 inch laptop out there, with an amazing battery life, but I had too many issues with it and ended up returning it.  The main pros were the weight and battery life, but here are the cons:1. speaker is barely audible - i have to put the speaker close to my ears to hear what someone is saying if I'm playing say a TED talk2. This could very well just have been the unit I got but the space bar wouldn't work every other tap or so, so i ended up typing sentences that looked like this for e.g. "hi therehoware you doing itwas so good toseeyou" and it was super time consuming having to go back to add the spaces.3. The screen is very reflective and was hurting my eyes - I came from a matte mac and it was very comfy on the eyes, this one gave me eye strain and even after buying one of those blue light filtered glasses it still was straining. I ended up buying (and am really liking) the Samsung Notebook 9 because I read it has a matte-reflective hybrid and I have found pretty much the perfect laptop for me - 15 inches (note that the LG gram is still a bit bigger at 15.6 and the Samsung is only 15) but with a comfortable matte like screen, and still pretty light, under 3 pounds, although not as light as the LG Gram. i do find the LG Gram aesthetically more pleasing but I guess there is still no absolutely perfect laptop for me, not yet anyway.4. The cursor seems to have a mind of it's own and I can be typing and all of a sudden section of words get highlighted and deleted - I am assuming it must be a hyper sensitive touchpad but even adjusting the touchpad settings didn't really help much5.  The camera placement is at the bottom of the screen so the person I'm talking to would be looking up my chin and nostril - ugh. SUPER unflattering.Overall this was a great looking laptop and the weight was it's phenomenal plus, and I thought it was more affordable than the Samsung but the too reflective screen and space key working only part time and the jumpy cursor were what made me decide I couldn't live with this happily for the next 3-4 years. I actually am having a bit of PTSD now even with my new Samsung, thinking every so often that ok something's gonna get deleted...or the spaces are not gonna show up - but nope! working perfectly and I am super pleased with it.

review_title: This is a great machine with one fatal design flaw
review_text: This is a great machine with one fatal design flaw, which really hit me unexpectedly once I got it last week and started using it.The keyboard is centered about two inches to the left of the middle of the trackpad. When you are typing, your palm will occasionally brush the trackpad, causing the mouse pointer to jump to somewhere else in the document or thread you are working on.Maybe I have fat palms, but dang if this isn't the most annoying thing I've encountered this week. :/

I only have ~12 hours of battery life, which is about a half of what they have promised. It still lasts 3 times longer than my current Thinkpad, though.  Otherwise, I love light weight, slick design and crisp screen of this LG laptop. My previous laptop was X1Carbon, and this is a hugh upgrade.Only after a few days of use though, the software and hardware seem quite stable. No single blue screen of death yet. I swapped the SSD to Samsung NVME PM-951 and the laptop is running like Usain Bolt.I also added 16gB DDR4 SO-DIMM memory into a slot. There was only one slot there. The laptop came with 8gB RAM preinstalled (soldered on board somewhere), so now I have 24gB RAM recognized by the OS. Now I carefully monitoring any impact of this on the battery life of the laptop.

review_title: Excellent laptop.  Very powerful and incredibly light
review_text: Excellent laptop.  Very powerful and incredibly light (just under 2 lbs).  People have told me that they have paper notebooks that weigh more than this computer.  The IT guy at work was amazed at how powerful it is - he said that it normally takes about 20 mins to load Win 10 operating system on a typical machine and this laptop installed it in about 5 mins!  The light weight advantage and the power were the main reasons I chose this computer.  I travel a lot and got sick and tired of lugging around a Dell brick.As for the cons:- the power cord connection into the socket on the side is tight and tiny.  I would have preferred something smoother - like a Dell.- The track-pad is not the best.  It's quite functional and I would give it a 8/10, but it does require a bit more pressure than I would like to click the left and right buttons... less pressure than a two year old Toshiba, and slightly more pressure than a Dell XPS15.  However, I mostly use a mouse rather than the track-pad, so it doesn't bother me that much.  This reminds me of another concern - the default setting locks the track-pad when you insert a dongle receiver for your mouse.  There's a simple setting to enable the track-pad so you can use your finger on the pad and use the mouse simultaneously.  Otherwise, you will have to remove the dongle in order to use your finger on the pad.For the above two reasons, I wanted to give the gram 4 1/2 stars, but a half star was not an option, and this is still an incredible laptop.I've read others say that it runs hot, and I fully expected it when I saw the power it pushes.  However, I was pleasantly surprised to find that this is not true.  My daughter has a Dell XPS15 and it runs so hot that she must always have a cooling fan under it while on her lap.  The gram runs slightly warm, and substantially less heat than I expected... very negligibly noticeable.  And with the solid state drive, there's no fan blowing hot air at you all the time.  The SSD is also incredible - very fast boot-ups and shut downs.If you can believe, the chief concern I have is the fear of dropping it when holding it between my arm and side while washing my hands in a public restroom while I'm traveling and have it out of it's case.  It is so amazingly thin and light that you really have to exert some clamping pressure with your arm so it doesn't slide away.The screen resolution is brilliant and there are pop up suggestions to dim the screen to save battery.  I mostly have it plugged in on a desk top, so I keep the brightness set high to enjoy the quality picture.  I multi-task like crazy and often have as many as 12 tabs open at a time in Chrome - not a problem whatsoever... as I said earlier, it's a powerful  chip and memory configuration.  All in all a very sweet machine.  A tad expensive, but well worth it if power and a light weight design are a priority.February 15, 2018 Update:  The gram is still blowing me away.  This is without a doubt a superior selection over a Zenbook or a Dell XPS.  I marvel at how fast this machine boots up after loading all my other software - I clocked it at 8 seconds to fully boot up.  I wish my desktop had this speed, and it's a Dell Workstation with a Xeon chip and 16 GB of RAM w/a SSD for the operating system.  The gram still runs cool - no overheating ever, and the sound system is quite acceptable for videos, news, etc.  My compliments to LG for packing all this power into such a slim and lightweight laptop.

Overall, I would recommend this laptop. I think the thing that holds me back from a full 5 stars is the SSD size and the quality of the laptop material, but it's not that big of a deal personally.Pros:-Lightweight... slightly redundant.-Screen looks pretty good to my eye.-Mouse pad seems fairly responsive and has tactile clicks.-Two levels of back light for the keyboard.-Good battery life.-Runs cool and quiet.Cons:-The material feels slightly cheap, but not potato laptop cheap. It's probably the price for being lightweight. Still feels decent to me.-Webcam position is bad, but doesn't matter personally. Quality is normal laptop quality.-Speakers are subpar, but I suppose that's what you get with a thin and light laptop.As a father's day gift for my dad, I was looking for high end laptops running Windows. Hardware wise, I was looking for 8GB ram minimum, highest storage of SSD possible near a $1000 budget, 6-8 hours of battery minimum, runs cool and quiet, and less than 5lbs. I'm not too crazy on resolution or touch screen since me nor my dad would make use of that or care about higher resolution when it already looks decent (and higher resolution will usually lower overall battery life). I got the non-touch screen i5 version with a 1080p screen.This laptop is really only for typical applications like Microsoft Office, Chrome, Spotify, movie watching, etc. You could probably do some audio recording with this because it's basically inaudible and runs super cool. (Can't remember if it's passively cooled or not...) But for gaming, look for a different laptop with a dedicated GPU, and for video editing you'll probably want more onboard storage and maybe 16GB of ram. 512GB of storage would've been preferable for me, but with SSDs on laptops right now it's expensive. I was keeping an eye out for USB-C ports too since that will become a standard soon, if not already. Also, under the description it can be easily missed, but the laptop size is actually 14.1" across. The small bezels and rectangular build makes it this way, so the footprint is smaller than other 15.6" inch screen laptops.I was considering the Dell XPS 13/15, Asus Zenbook 3, Surface Laptop, a few models of Lenovo, and others, but mostly the XPS 15 and Surface laptop. I decided against the XPS because I saw a lot of quality control and customer service issues in reviews, even though many YouTube reviewers highly recommended it. I decided against the Surface laptop because it was a good couple hundred dollars more for for similar hardware specs, a lack of USB-C, and the unknown quality of how long the alcantara will last. I also figured we didn't need a 2:3 aspect ratio, and a 16:9 would probably be more standard.

Couldn't be happier with this svelte laptop.  It's thinness and clean design make it look fantastic.  I chose it for its minimal weight, but it is also has more than sufficient computing power. I primarily use it for CAD, so the full number pad on the keyboard is a bonus.  The battery life is certainly impressive.  It's not my primary computer, so I'm not not using it for 8 hours a day (more like an hour here or there each day), but I typically go several days without having to recharge it.  I could see the strange position of the webcam being an issue if I ever used it, but I don't.  Really my only complaint, as others have noted, is that the screen could stand to be a little brighter.  I usually find myself turning it up to full brightness, even indoors.UPDATE:I was excited about the purported ability of this laptop to be charged via its USB-C port.  I figured I could get a USB-A to USB-C cord, and be able to charge my laptop via the same transformer as my phone and eliminate carrying the laptop's original transformer around.  Even better, I'd be able to charge my Gram on the go via my car's USB outlet, or on the plane using the seatback USB outlets, or using my portable power bank.  I assumed it might charge a little slower since it's not as beefy a transformer, and I was ok with that.Unfortunately, that's not the case.  I've learned that in order to charge the Gram via its USB-C port, its has to be connected to a 20volt/2amp source.  USB-A ports max out at around 5volts/2amps.  Since I don't have any other devices that use USB-C yet (and neither do my car or any planes I've seen), it renders this feature irrelevant.Not sure if this is a limitation of all laptops with USB-C charging, or a restriction LG decided to impose for some reason.  It's still a great laptop, and I'm not taking off any stars, but I thought other buyers should know.

review_title: Great Little PC for running Citrix on Linux
review_text: What a great little computer!!! I bought this for the primary reason of working remotely from home using Citrix Workspace.I read on other reviews about how much space Windows 10 needs, especially for updates, and immediately had the intention of installing netrunner Core Linux  and erasing Windows.If you plan on doing the same thing, word of advice if you need the wifi to work... make sure to boot into Windows first and copy the 4345r6nvram.txt file from system32/drivers to a thumb drive. Once you have Linux installed, copy the txt file to lib/firmware/brcm/brcmfmac43455-sdio.txt using the sudo cp command. Then, you need to unload the module using rmmod brcmfmac and load it again using modprobe brcmfmac.Once I got the actual icaclient Linux application installed, I had to download the Digicert Global Root G2 and sudo cp to opt/Citrix/ICAClient/keystore/cacerts. Then, after running ctx_rehash, it worked like a charm. I honestly prefer this than using the Google Chrome add-on.I've used Citrix Workspace for two days so far and I've had absolutely no issues. I have to use my web browser to get the ica file but once I selected open this file type always, it launches the icaclient.Next on the list was installing my nes, snes and Sega emulators. That's when things got a little weird. After exiting the nes and snes emulators, I had to readjust the screen resolution. And once I did that, the behavior of the file manager was strange. It was as if it crashed and to fix it, I had to log off and back on. Oh, well.YouTube and Prime Video played pretty good using the Google Chrome browser. There was a slight skipping during a car driving scene on Prime Video but it was barely noticeable.After a whole day's use, it didn't really heat up that much. Only a slight warmness. While streaming, it got a little warmer. Not going to use it much for that, though.Overall, I'm completely satisfied with my purchase and would highly recommend it to anyone willing to take the Linux plunge.

review_title: *Grad Student Review* Stable channel compatible for Google Play, super lightweight and thin, sleek, and fast performing...
review_text: I am working on my 2nd Masters degree (I know, I'm nuts) and my 3rd laptop in five years crapped out (Dell, HP, and Dell again). I don't know if I am just tough on my laptops or what but they only last just slightly out of the warranty. I didn't want to spend a ton of money on a laptop that will be gathering dust after next year (YAY, 4th graduation) and I wanted something sturdy, high quality, and useful for periodic web surfing and ebook/audiobooks once I no longer have assignments. I didn't consider Chromebooks at first but nearly everything I do is Google-based for work and school anyway. I ultimately chose this model because it seemed to have better reported performance and quality that Chromebooks around $200. I specifically looked for Chromebooks listed as compatible with Google Play in the "stable channel" because I read that beta channel compatibility was problematic and some other Chromebooks aren't compatible yet at all. You can google the list of stable channel compatible chromebooks if this is important to you.  Anyway, I have been able to download most of the apps I am used to having on my Android phone, iPad, and Kindle Fire and use them without issue. I think its worth it to spend a little extra money to have the convertibility, compatibility, and better performance. Big plus is the Chromebook weighs a lot less and is a lot thinner than my last laptop so I am looking forward to a lighter, less bulky bag. The keyboard and buttons are larger than I expected and my average sized hands do not feel crowded using it. I have bought a few extra accessories through Amazon to help make this work for my use: glass screen protectors, a felt sleeve, a samsung 32GB mini SD card, and a Type C to USB adapter.I do have two concerns that will have to wait until I get back into classes in late August: how well the chromebook allows me to utilize Microsoft Word and Excel for course work and how compatible it is with my school's new LMS (Learning Management System), BrightSpace. I'll report back on any issues I notice with these.For now, I am extremely happy with my purchase.
